parameter.name: PacketDA
parameter.description:
The Destination Address (DA) for the packets in this flow.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfPacketDA'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: MaxRate
parameter.description:
Maximum required rate in {{units}}.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfPeakDataRate'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: MaxBurstSize
parameter.description:
Maximum burst size.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfBurstSize'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: LeaseTime
parameter.description:
Flow lease time (expressed in {{units}}).
A {{param}} of 0 means unlimited lease time.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfLeaseTime'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: Tag
parameter.description: The FLOW_TAG of the PQoS flow identified by {{param|FlowID}} in which this MoCA interface is an Ingress Node for this PQoS flow. The FLOW_TAG carries application specific content of this PQoS flow. See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|Section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: LeaseTimeLeft
parameter.description:
Flow lease time remaining (expressed in {{units}}).
If {{param|LeaseTime}} is 0 then a {{param}} of 0 means unlimited lease time; otherwise, a {{param}} of 0 means expired.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfLeaseTimeLeft'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: FlowPackets
parameter.description:
The number of packets transmitted for this flow.
This parameter is based on ''mocaIfTxPacketsFlow'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: IngressGuid
parameter.description:
The MAC address of the MoCA Node specified by the INGRESS_NODE_ID parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|Section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: EgressGuid
parameter.description:
The MAC address of the MoCA Node specified by the EGRESS_NODE_ID parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: MaximumLatency
parameter.description:
The MAXIMUM_LATENCY parameter of the flow in units of milliseconds. A value of 0 indicates no value available.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: ShortTermAvgRatio
parameter.description:
The SHORT_TERM_AVERAGE_RATIO parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: FlowPer
parameter.description:
The FLOW_PER parameter of this flow, where a value of 0 indicates NPER and 1 indicates VLPER.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: IngressClassify
parameter.description:
The INGRESS_CLASSIFICATION_RULE parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: VlanTag
parameter.description:
The VLAN_TAG parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: DscpMoca
parameter.description:
The DSCP_MOCA parameter of the flow.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 6.3.13.1}}.

parameter.name: Dfid
parameter.description:
The destination flow ID of the flow assigned by the Ingress Node.
See {{bibref|MoCAv2.0|section 7.8.1.2}}.

object.name: Device.MoCA.Interface.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.
object.description:
This table contains information about other MoCA devices currently associated with this MoCA interface.
Entries in this table cannot be created or deleted by the network management system. All entries are created or deleted by the device software.

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description: The MAC address of the associated device's MoCA interface.

parameter.name: NodeID
parameter.description:
The Node ID of this remote device.
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeIndex'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: PreferredNC
parameter.description:
Whether this remote device is a preferred Network Coordinator (NC).
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodePreferredNC'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: HighestVersion
PHYTxRate
parameter.description:
The PHY transmit rate (in {{units}}) to this remote device.
This parameter is based on ''mocaMeshTxRate'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.
This parameter MUST NOT be implemented for MoCA 2.0 because it doesn't map to a MIB object.

parameter.name: PHYRxRate
parameter.description:
The PHY receive rate (in {{units}}) from this remote device.
This parameter MUST NOT be implemented for MoCA 2.0 because it doesn't map to a MIB object.

parameter.name: TxPowerControlReduction
RxPowerLevel
TxBcastRate
parameter.description:
The broadcast PHY transmit rate from this remote device.
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeTxGcdRate'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: RxBcastPowerLevel
parameter.description:
The power level received at the MoCA interface from this remote device.
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeRxGcdPower'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: TxPackets
parameter.description: The number of packets transmitted to this remote device (Note: Includes Broadcast, Multicast and Unicast packets).

parameter.name: TxDrops
parameter.description: The number of Unicast EPDUs received at the ECL, destined to the associated MoCA Node, and not transmitted by this MoCA interface.

parameter.name: RxPackets
parameter.description:
The number of packets received from this remote device (Note: Includes Broadcast, Multicast and Unicast packets).
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeRxPackets'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: RxCorrected
parameter.description: The number of Ethernet packets received by this MoCA interface that have errors and are corrected from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: RxErroredAndMissedPackets
parameter.description:
The number of errored and missed packets received from this remote device.
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeRxDrops'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.

parameter.name: BondingCapable
parameter.description: The MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} supports Bonding if the value is {{true}}. The MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} does not support Bonding if this value is {{false}}.

parameter.name: QAM256Capable
parameter.description:
Whether this remote device supports the 256 QAM feature.
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodeQAM256Capable'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.
This parameter MUST NOT be implemented for MoCA 2.0 because it doesn't map to a MIB object.

parameter.name: PacketAggregationCapability
parameter.description:
The packet aggregation capability supported by the remote device. Standard values are 0 (no support), 6 (6 {{units}}) or 10 (10 {{units}}).
This parameter is based on ''mocaNodePacketsAggrCapability'' from {{bibref|MOCA11-MIB}}.
Note that this parameter maps to different MIB objects for MoCA 1.0/1.1 and MoCA 2.0. [XXX2: Need to modify the syntax to 'unsignedInt' because MoCA 2.0 requires a minimum of 20 packets and MoCA 2.5 requires a minimum of 80 packets.]

parameter.name: RxSNR
Active
parameter.description:
Whether or not this remote device is currently present in the MoCA network.
The ability to list inactive nodes is OPTIONAL. If the CPE includes inactive nodes in this table, {{param}} MUST be set to {{false}} for each inactive node. The length of time an inactive node remains listed in this table is a local matter to the CPE.

parameter.name: SupportedIngressPqosFlows
parameter.description: The number of Ingress PQoS Flows supported by this MoCA interface from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: SupportedEgressPqosFlows
parameter.description: The number of Egress PQoS Flows supported by this MoCA interface from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: AggregationSize
parameter.description: The maximum number of bytes that can be aggregated in a MoCA frame that this MoCA Node supports.

parameter.name: AeNumber
parameter.description: The maximum number of allocation elements, excluding the TAUs and the Dummy DAUs, in one MAP that this MoCA Node supports.

parameter.name: PowerState
parameter.description: Power State of the MoCA Node identified by the {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: PowerStateCapability
parameter.description: Power State capability of the MoCA Node identified by the {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: PDelay
parameter.description: Propagation delay measured in units of 10ns between the local MoCA Node and the MoCA Node identified by the {{param|MACAddress}}.

parameter.name: EnhancedPrivacyCapable
parameter.description: Indicates the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} supports MoCA 2 Enhanced Privacy if the value is {{true}}. Indicates the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} does not support MoCA 2 Enhanced Privacy if this value is {{false}}.

parameter.name: LinkType
parameter.description: Indicates the type of link used for unicast data transmissions between the managed MoCA Node and the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}.

enumeration.description: MoCA 1 PHY.
Primary.
Bonded.
300 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY.
400 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY.
500 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY.

parameter.name: Moca25PhyCapable
parameter.description: Indicates the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} supports MoCA 2.5 PHY if the value is {{true}}. Indicates the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} does not support MoCA 2.5 PHY if this value is {{false}}.

parameter.name: RxPwrList
parameter.description:
Per channel list of Receive power levels in dBm from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} to the managed MoCA Node.
The power measurement should cover the preamble and/or at least a symbol time. The averaging method employed for this measurement is implementation specific and not specified. It is recommended but not required to utilize the LMO (Link Maintenance Operation) EVM probes for this measurement.
The field numValues is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* MoCA 1 PHY - 1
* Primary - 1
* Bonded - 2
* 300 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 3
* 400 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 4
* 500 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 5
struct moca25NodePowerList { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) struct { char power; // 1 octet (Rx Power Level in dBm) } [numValues]; };

parameter.name: RxSNRList
parameter.description:
Per channel list of Average Receive Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) across all available subcarriers based on the EVM probe from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}} to the managed MoCA Node.
The field numValues is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* MoCA 1 PHY - 1
* Primary - 1
* Bonded - 2
* 300 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 3
* 400 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 4
* 500 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 5
struct moca25NodeRxSNRList { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) struct { char snr; // 1 octet (Rx SNR in dB) } [numValues]; };

parameter.name: TxPwrList
parameter.description:
Per channel list of Transmit power levels in dBm from the managed MoCA Node to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}. The transmit power should be max power for the channel less the Transmit Power Control.
The field numValues is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* MoCA 1 PHY - 1
* Primary - 1
* Bonded - 2
* 300 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 3
* 400 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 4
* 500 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 5
struct moca25NodePowerList { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) struct { char power; // 1 octet (Tx Power Level in dBm) } [numValues]; };

parameter.name: TxPwrReductionList
parameter.description:
Per channel list of Transmit Power Control (TPC) back-off in dB used for unicast transmissions from the managed MoCA Node to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|MACAddress}}.
{{param}} is identical to the TPC back-off utilized for transmission from the TPC backoff parameter TX_POWER_ADJUSTMENT_100MHZ.
The field numValues is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* MoCA 1 PHY - 1
* Primary - 1
* Bonded - 2
* 300 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 3
* 400 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 4
* 500 MHz MoCA 2.5 PHY - 5
struct moca25NodeTxPwrReductionList { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) struct { char tpc; // 1 octet (TPC in dB) } [numValues]; };

parameter.name: EgressNodeNumFlows
parameter.description: The number of PQoS flows in which this MoCA interface is an Egress Node for these PQoS flows.

parameter.name: IngressNodeNumFlows
parameter.description: The number of PQoS flows in which this MoCA interface is an Ingress Node for these PQoS flows.

object.name: Device.MoCA.Interface.{i}.Mesh.{i}.
object.description:
MoCA mesh PHY rate table. This table contains the unicast transmit PHY rate between all pairs of MoCA Nodes in the MoCA network.
Since {{param|TxRate}} is the transmit PHY rate from {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to {{param|RxNodeIndex}}, this table does not contain any entries with {{param|TxNodeIndex}} equals {{param|RxNodeIndex}}. In addition, a MoCA network can have less than 16 Nodes, hence some values of {{param|TxNodeIndex}} and {{param|RxNodeIndex}} in the range of 0 to 15 may not exist.
Entries in this table cannot be created or deleted by the network management system. All entries are created or deleted by the device software.

parameter.name: TxNodeIndex
parameter.description: The Node ID of the transmit MoCA Node is used as one of the index to order the mesh PHY rate table.

parameter.name: RxNodeIndex
parameter.description: The Node ID of the receive MoCA Node is used as one of the index to order the mesh PHY rate table.

parameter.name: TxRate
parameter.description: The transmit MoCA 1 PHY rate in Mbps from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}.

parameter.name: TxRateNper
parameter.description: The transmit normal packet error PHY Rate from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}.

parameter.name: TxRateVlper
parameter.description: The transmit very low packet error PHY Rate from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}.

parameter.name: LinkType
parameter.description:
The type of link which exists from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}. {{enum}}
This parameter is only used for MoCA 2.0.

parameter.name: Power
parameter.description:
Per channel list of Transmit or Receive power levels in dBm. If the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} is equal to {{param|#.NodeID}}, then indicates the unicast transmit power in dBm from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}, else indicates the unicast receive power in dBm from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} at the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}.
For transmit power, the power should be max power for the channel less the Transmit Power Control. For received power, the power measurement should cover the preamble and/or at least a symbol time. The averaging method employed for this measurement is implementation specific and not specified. It is recommended but not required to utilize the LMO (Link Maintenance Operation) EVM probes for this measurement.
The field ''numValues'' is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* {{enum|moca1PHY|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|primary|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|bonded|LinkType}} - 2
struct mocaPower { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) { char power; // 1 octet (Tx or Rx Power Level in dB) } [numValues]; };
This parameter is only used for MoCA 2.0.

parameter.name: PowerReduction
parameter.description:
Per channel list of The Transmit Power Control (TPC) back-off in dB. If the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} is equal to {{param|#.NodeID}}, then indicates the TPC in dB utilized to back-off transmission to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}}. Otherwise indicates the TPC in dB that the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} utilized to back-off its transmission.
{{param}} is identical to the TPC back-off utilized for transmission and determined from the TPC backoff parameters TPC_BACKOFF_MAJOR and TPC_BACKOFF_MINOR as follows: {{param}} = TPC_BACKOFF_MAJOR * 3 +TPC_BACKOFF_MINOR.
The field ''numValues'' is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* {{enum|moca1PHY|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|primary|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|bonded|LinkType}} - 2
struct mocaPowerReduction { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) { char tpc; // 1 octet (TPC in dB) } [numValues]; };
This parameter is only used for MoCA 2.0.

parameter.name: RxSNR
parameter.description:
Per channel list of average received Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) in dB. If the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}} is not equal to {{param|#.NodeID}} or the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} is equal to {{param|#.NodeID}}, then this parameter is not present. Otherwise indicates the average received SNR across all the available carriers based on the EVM probe from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}}.
The field ''numValues'' is a function of {{param|LinkType}}:
* {{enum|moca1PHY|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|primary|LinkType}} - 1
* {{enum|bonded|LinkType}} - 2
struct mocaRxSNR { char numValues; // 1 octet (Number of Values to follow) { char rx_snr; // 1 octet (Rx SNR in dB) } [numValues]; };
This parameter is only used for MoCA 2.0.

object.name: Device.MoCA.Interface.{i}.Bridge.{i}.
object.description:
MoCA bridge Ethernet MAC address table. This table contains an entry for every MoCA Node in the MoCA network.
Entries in this table cannot be created or deleted by the network management system. All entries are created or deleted by the device software.

parameter.name: NodeIndex
parameter.description: The Node ID is used as an index to order the MAC entries in the MoCA bridge table.

parameter.name: MACAddresses
parameter.description: The Ethernet MAC addresses identified by the Node ID.

object.name: Device.MoCA.Interface.{i}.MeshScMod.{i}.
object.description:
MoCA mesh Subcarrier Modulation table. This table contains the Unicast transmit subcarrier modulation between all pairs of MoCA Nodes in the MoCA network.
Since {{param|Mod}} is the subcarrier modulation from {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to {{param|RxNodeIndex}}, this table does not contain any entries with {{param|TxNodeIndex}} equals {{param|RxNodeIndex}}. In addition, a MoCA network can have less than 16 MoCA Nodes, hence some values of {{param|TxNodeIndex}} and {{param|RxNodeIndex}} in the range of 0 to 15 may not exist. The {{param|ChannelIndex}} index is used to differentiate between the primary and secondary channels in a bonded channel network. The primary channel index is always present, the secondary channel index may not always be present.
Entries in this table cannot be created or deleted by the network management system. All entries are created or deleted by the device software.

parameter.name: TxNodeIndex
parameter.description: The Node ID of the transmit MoCA Node is used as one of the index to order the mesh PHY rate table.

parameter.name: RxNodeIndex
parameter.description: The Node ID of the receive MoCA Node is used as one of the index to order the mesh subcarrier modulation.

parameter.name: ChannelIndex
parameter.description:
{{enum|primary}} or {{enum|secondary}} channel for MoCA 2.0 Node associated with {{param|Nper}} and {{param|Vlper}}. For MoCA 1 Node, the same as the {{enum|primary}} channel associated with {{param|Mod}}. In a bonded MoCA 2.0 network, the {{enum|primary}} and {{enum|secondary}} channels each have their own subcarrier modulation data.
{{enum|m25first}}, {{enum|m25second}}, {{enum|m25third}}, {{enum|m25fourth}} or {{enum|m25fifth}} channel for MoCA 2.5 Node associated with {{param|ModM25}}.

parameter.name: Mod
parameter.description: 1 Byte Hex array values with no delimiters where each byte indicates the subcarrier modulation of one subcarrier from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}} for the MoCA 1 Unicast transmission PHY profile.

parameter.name: Nper
parameter.description: 1 Byte Hex array values with no delimiters where each byte indicates the unicast NPER subcarrier modulation of one subcarrier from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}} for the associated {{param|ChannelIndex}}.

parameter.name: Vlper
parameter.description: 1 Byte Hex array values with no delimiters where each byte indicates the unicast VLPER subcarrier modulation of one subcarrier from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}} for the associated {{param|ChannelIndex}}.

parameter.name: ModM25
parameter.description:
1 Byte Hex array values with no delimiters where each byte indicates the MoCA 2.5 unicast subcarrier modulation for all subcarriers from the MoCA Node identified by {{param|TxNodeIndex}} to the MoCA Node identified by {{param|RxNodeIndex}} for the associated {{param|ChannelIndex}}.
For MoCA 2.5 First Channel, Second Channel, Third Channel, Fourth Channel and Fifth Channel, the total number of subcarriers is 512.

object.name: Device.Ghn.
object.description: G.hn object that contains an {{object|Interface}} table for G.hn supported CPE. The ITU-T G.hn specifications {{bibref|G.9960}} and {{bibref|G.9961}} define Physical and MAC Layers for communication between two or more G.hn nodes in the home network over multiple wired media such as power line, phone line and coaxial cable.

parameter.name: InterfaceNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.
object.description: G.hn interface table (a stackable interface object as described in {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2}}). Each table entry models the PHY {{bibref|G.9960}} and MAC {{bibref|G.9961}} layers of a G.hn interface.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description:
Enables or disables the interface.
This parameter is based on ''ifAdminStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
The current operational state of the interface (see {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.2}}). {{enum}}
When {{param|Enable}} is {{false}} then {{param}} SHOULD normally be {{enum|Down}} (or {{enum|NotPresent}} or {{enum|Error}} if there is a fault condition on the interface).
When {{param|Enable}} is changed to {{true}} then {{param}} SHOULD change to {{enum|Up}} if and only if the interface is able to transmit and receive network traffic; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Dormant}} if and only if the interface is operable but is waiting for external actions before it can transmit and receive network traffic (and subsequently change to {{enum|Up}} if still operable when the expected actions have completed); it SHOULD change to {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} if and only if the interface is prevented from entering the {{enum|Up}} state because one or more of the interfaces beneath it is down; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|Error}} state if there is an error or other fault condition detected on the interface; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|NotPresent}} state if the interface has missing (typically hardware) components; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Unknown}} if the state of the interface can not be determined for some reason.
This parameter is based on ''ifOperStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.
Because the interface includes layer 1, the {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} value SHOULD never be used.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: The textual name of the interface as assigned by the CPE.

parameter.name: LastChange
parameter.description: The accumulated time in {{units}} since the interface entered its current operational state.

parameter.name: LowerLayers
parameter.description:
{{list}} {{reference|an interface object that is stacked immediately below this interface object}} See {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.1}}.
Note: Since {{object}} is a layer 1 interface, it is expected that {{param}} will not be used.

parameter.name: Upstream
parameter.description:
Indicates whether the interface points towards the Internet ({{true}}) or towards End Devices ({{false}}).
For example:
* For an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all WAN interfaces and {{false}} for all LAN interfaces.
* For a standalone WiFi Access Point that is connected via Ethernet to an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for the Ethernet interface and {{false}} for the WiFi Radio interface.
* For an End Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all interfaces.

parameter.name: MaxBitRate
parameter.description: The maximum upstream and downstream PHY bit rate supported by this interface (expressed in {{units}}).

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description:
The MAC Address of the interface, denoted as node MAC address or REGID in {{bibref|G.9961}}.
Note: This is not necessarily the same as the Ethernet header source or destination MAC address, which is associated with the IP interface and is modeled via the {{param|##.Ethernet.Link.{i}.MACAddress}} parameter.

parameter.name: FirmwareVersion
parameter.description: The firmware version of the interface.

parameter.name: ConnectionType
MaxTransmitRate
parameter.description: The maximum PHY data rate that the interface is capable of transmitting (expressed in {{units}}).

parameter.name: TargetDomainNames
parameter.description: {{list}} Identifies the target domains configured by the user, as described in {{bibref|G.9961|Section 8.6.1}}. When registering or re-registering, the G.hn interface SHOULD try to register to one of these domains in the given order.

parameter.name: DomainName
parameter.description:
This is the domain name to which the interface is currently registered.
{{empty}} indicates that the interface is currently not registered.

parameter.name: DomainNameIdentifier
parameter.description: The Domain Name Identifier, a shortened version of {{param|DomainName}}, denoted as DNI in {{bibref|G.9961|Section 8.6.11.2.1}}.

parameter.name: DomainId
parameter.description: The Domain Identifier of the domain to which the interface is registered, denoted as DOD in {{bibref|G.9961}}.

parameter.name: DeviceId
parameter.description:
The Device Identifier assigned by the Domain Master, denoted as DEVICE_ID in {{bibref|G.9961}}.
The value 0 indicates that the device is not currently registered.

parameter.name: NodeTypeDMCapable
parameter.description: Indicates whether this interface has the capability to act as Domain Master in the G.hn domain.

parameter.name: DMRequested
parameter.description: Indicates a request to force the role of the G.hn interface to Domain Master (DM) for the G.hn domain it is connected to. The selection of the Domain Master follows the procedures described in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.6.6}}.

parameter.name: IsDM
parameter.description: Indicates whether this G.hn interface is currently the Domain Master (DM) for the G.hn domain it is connected to, as described in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.6}}.

parameter.name: NodeTypeSCCapable
parameter.description: Indicates whether this interface has the capability to act as Security Controller in the G.hn domain.

parameter.name: SCRequested
parameter.description: Indicates a request to force the role of the G.hn interface to Security Controller (SC) for the G.hn domain it is connected to. The selection of the Security Controller follows the procedures described in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 9.2}}.

parameter.name: IsSC
parameter.description: Indicates whether this G.hn interface is currently the Security Controller (SC) for the G.hn domain it is connected to, as described in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 9.2}}.

parameter.name: StandardVersions
parameter.description:
The standard versions that the interface supports. The list MUST have an even number of items. The first item of each pair represents an ITU-T G.hn Recommendation while the second element of each pair represents the amendment version of the indicated Recommendation that this interface supports (the value 0 corresponds to the base Recommendation).
For example, to indicate support for the G.9960 base document and G.9961 amendment 1, the corresponding list would be "G9960,0,G9961,1".

parameter.name: MaxBandPlan
parameter.description: The largest bandplan that the interface can support, as defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.8.5.5}}.

parameter.name: MediumType
parameter.description: The medium type that the interface currently operates on. Refer to {{bibref|G.9962|Table 7-5}}.

parameter.name: TAIFG
parameter.description: The Acknowledgement InterFrame Gap, or TAIFG, as defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.4}}. It is represented as multiples of {{units}}.

parameter.name: NotchedAmateurRadioBands
parameter.description:
A bit map representing usage of international amateur bands (0 = masked, 1 = unmasked). The LSB represents the lowest band (1.8-2.0 MHz), the second LSB represents the second lowest band (3.5-4.0 MHz), and so on. The maximum value for this parameter is 0x03FF, i.e. it is a 10-bit quantity represented in 16 bits and the top 6 bits are always zero.
International Radio amateur bands are described in {{bibref|G.9964|Table D-1}} and conveyed by the Domain Master in the Amateur radio band descriptor (see {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-77}}).

parameter.name: PHYThroughputDiagnosticsEnable
parameter.description:
{{nolist}}
Comma-separated list of DeviceIDs of nodes that need to enable their PHY throughput diagnostics mode. All devices that are enabled will participate in the G.hn network PHY throughput diagnostics process.

parameter.name: PerformanceMonitoringDiagnosticsEnable
parameter.description:
{{nolist}}
Comma-separated list of DeviceIDs of nodes that need to enable their Performance Monitoring diagnostics mode on this node. All devices that are enabled will participate in the G.hn network Performance Monitoring diagnostics process.

parameter.name: SMMaskedBandNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: NodeTypeDMConfig
parameter.description:
Requests the interface to become the Domain Master in the G.hn domain.
This parameter is valid only if {{param|NodeTypeDMCapable}} is {{true}}.
Note that, if more than one node is configured to act as Domain Master, G.hn specifies a protocol to ensure only one device actually becomes DM.

parameter.name: NodeTypeDMStatus
parameter.description:
Indicates whether the interface is acting as Domain Master ({{true}}) or not ({{false}}).
See Note in {{param|NodeTypeDMConfig}} regarding the possibility of more than one node being configured with {{param|NodeTypeDMConfig}} = {{true}}.

parameter.name: NodeTypeSCStatus
parameter.description: Indicates whether the interface is acting as Security Controller ({{true}}) or not ({{false}}).

parameter.name: AssociatedDeviceNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: PSM

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.Stats.
object.description:
Throughput statistics for this interface at the different G.hn reference points described in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1}}.
The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's {{param|#.Status}} parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's {{param|#.Enable}} parameter transitions from {{false}} to {{true}}). Administrative and operational interface status is discussed in {{bibref|TR-181i2|section 4.2.2}}.

command.name: Reset()
command.description: Reset all this object's statistics counters to zero.

parameter.name: BytesSent
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} transmitted out of the interface, including framing characters.
More specifically, this is the total number of MPDU bytes transmitted or retransmitted by the node through a physical medium (i.e., PMI defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}), which correspond to data LPDUs (i.e., data packets) and framing overhead (e.g., LFH, LPH, LPCS defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1}}). It does not include transmitted bytes contributed by management LPDUs (i.e., management packets).
Note: LPDUs in mixed LLC frame blocks are considered data LPDUs.

parameter.name: BytesReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} received on the interface, including framing characters.
More specifically, this is the total number of MPDU bytes received by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to data LPDUs and framing overhead. It does not include received bytes contributed by management LPDUs. It can include blocks with errors.
Note: LPDUs in mixed LLC frame blocks are considered data LPDUs.

parameter.name: PacketsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} transmitted out of the interface.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}) that were transmitted by the node through the physical medium. It does not include transmitted LCDUs.

parameter.name: PacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} received on the interface.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) that were received by the node through the physical medium. It does not include received LCDUs.

parameter.name: ErrorsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of outbound {{units}} that could not be transmitted because of errors.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}) but could not be transmitted because of errors (e.g., APDUs containing CRC errors).

parameter.name: ErrorsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of inbound {{units}} that contained errors preventing them from being delivered to a higher-layer protocol.
More specifically, this is the total number of received APDUs that contained errors preventing them from being delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}). The possible causes of error are: incorrect CRC, incorrect MIC, incorrect MIC size, and incorrect size of packet.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} requested for transmission which were not addressed to a multicast or broadcast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a unicast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of outbound {{units}} which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being transmitted. One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) but chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being transmitted (e.g., buffer overflow).

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of inbound {{units}} which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being delivered. One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.
More specifically, this is the total number of received APDUs that were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being delivered.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} that higher-level protocols requested for transmission and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were not addressed to a multicast or broadcast address at this layer.
More specifically, this is the total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a unicast address at this layer.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer.
More specifically, this is the total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsSent
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} that higher-level protocols requested for transmission and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer.
More specifically, this is the total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer.

parameter.name: UnknownProtoPacketsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of {{units}} received via the interface which were discarded because of an unknown or unsupported protocol.
More specifically, this is the total number of APDUs received by the management that were discarded because of an unknown or unsupported protocol.

parameter.name: MgmtBytesSent
parameter.description: The total number of MPDU bytes transmitted by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to management LPDUs and framing overhead.

parameter.name: MgmtBytesReceived
parameter.description: The total number of MPDU bytes received by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to management LPDUs and framing overhead.

parameter.name: MgmtPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of LCDUs requested for transmission by a management layer (i.e., outbound LCDUs generated in LLC defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1.3}}) that were transmitted by the node through a physical medium.

parameter.name: MgmtPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of LCDUs delivered to a management layer (i.e., inbound LCDUs) that were received by the node through a physical medium.

parameter.name: BlocksSent
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were transmitted by the node through a physical medium, regardless of new or retransmitted LPDUs.

parameter.name: BlocksReceived
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were received by the node through a physical medium, with or without errors.

parameter.name: BlocksResent
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were retransmitted.

parameter.name: BlocksErrorsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of received LPDUs that contained errors.
Note the following relationships hold:
* PacketsSent + ErrorsSent + DiscardPacketsSent = UnicastPacketsSent + MulticastPacketsSent + BroadcastPacketsSent.
* PacketsReceived = UnicastPacketsReceived + MulticastPacketsReceived + BroadcastPacketsReceived.
* Retransmission rate = BlocksResent / BlocksSent.
* Block error rate = BlocksErrorReceived / BlocksReceived.

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.
object.description: This table contains information about other G.hn devices connected to this G.hn interface.

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description:
MAC address of remote G.hn device.
This is denoted as REGID in {{bibref|G.9961}}.

parameter.name: DeviceId
parameter.description: Device Id (as defined in G.hn) for the remote G.hn device, denoted as DEVICE_ID in {{bibref|G.9961}}.

parameter.name: TxPhyRate
parameter.description:
The PHY transmit Rate (expressed in {{units}}) to this remote device, denoted as PHY data rate in {{bibref|G.9961}}.
Refer to Note 1 of {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-48}}. To convert from the value in the table, divide by 32K (32768) and round down.

parameter.name: RxPhyRate
parameter.description:
The PHY receive Rate (expressed in {{units}}) from this remote device, denoted as PHY data rate in {{bibref|G.9961}}.
Refer to Note 1 of {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-48}}. To convert from the value in the table, divide by 32K (32768) and round down.

parameter.name: Active
parameter.description:
Whether or not this device is currently present in the G.hn domain.
The ability to list inactive nodes is OPTIONAL. If the CPE includes inactive nodes in this table, {{param}} MUST be set to {{false}} for each inactive node. The length of time an inactive node remains listed in this table is a local matter to the CPE.
If {{param}} is {{true}}, it indicates that the Status of the remote device is 0, 1, or 2 (see {{bibref|G.9961|Table 7-3}}).

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.DMInfo.
object.description: This object specifies management parameters pertaining to the domain functionality (Domain Master function; see {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.6}}). The object exists only on G.hn interfaces that are currently the Domain Master, i.e. for which parameter {{param|#.IsDM}} is {{true}}.

parameter.name: DomainName
parameter.description: This is the domain name to which the interface is currently registered. {{empty}} indicates that the interface is currently not registered.

parameter.name: DomainNameIdentifier
parameter.description: The Domain Name Identifier, a shortened version of {{param|DomainName}}, denoted as DNI in {{bibref|G.9961|Section 8.6.11.2.1}}.

parameter.name: DomainId
parameter.description: The Domain Identifier of the domain to which the interface is registered, denoted as DOD in {{bibref|G.9961}}.

parameter.name: MACCycleDuration
parameter.description: The MAC cycle duration, as specified in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.4}}. It is represented as multiples of {{units}}. In the case of power line, writing to this parameter has no effect and it reads back as 0, which is a special value indicating that the MAC cycle is synchronized with 2 AC cycles as defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.6.3.1}}.

parameter.name: SCDeviceId
parameter.description: The DEVICE_ID of the Security Controller selected by the Domain Master.

parameter.name: SCMACAddress
parameter.description: The REGID of the Security Controller selected by the Domain Master.

parameter.name: ReregistrationTimePeriod
parameter.description: The time interval for periodic re-registration, as specified in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.8.5.8}}. It is represented as multiples of {{units}}.

parameter.name: TopologyPeriodicInterval
parameter.description: The time interval that a node sends out the periodic topology update using TM_NodeTopologyChange.ind message, as specified in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.8.5.8.1}}. It is represented as multiples of {{units}}. The special value 0 represents an infinite interval (i.e., no periodic topology update).

parameter.name: MinSupportedBandplan
parameter.description: Indicates the value of the minimal bandplan capability for a node that is allowed to register to the domain.

parameter.name: MaxSupportedBandplan
parameter.description: Indicates the value of the minimal bandplan capability for a node that is allowed to register to the domain.

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.SCInfo.
object.description: This object specifies management parameters pertaining to the Security Controller functionality (Security Controller function; see {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 9.2}}). The object exists only on G.hn interfaces that are currently the Security Controller, i.e. for which parameter {{param|#.IsSC}} is {{true}}.

parameter.name: ModesSupported
parameter.description: The security modes that the Security Controller can support. Refer to {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 9.2}}.

enumeration.description: Node-to-Node
Network Membership Key

parameter.name: ModeEnabled
parameter.description: The security mode in which the Security Controller is operating.

parameter.name: MICSize
parameter.description: The selected MIC size used in the domain.

parameter.name: Location
parameter.description: Indicates whether the Security Controller is above the L1 reference point. It is set to {{true}} if the Security Controller is above the L1 reference point, and set to {{false}} otherwise.

object.name: Device.Ghn.Interface.{i}.SMMaskedBand.{i}.
object.description:
Specifies the list of masked bands to be applied to the G.hn interface. This information is conveyed by the Domain Master in the SM descriptor as specified in {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-77}}.
Instances of this object are expected to exist only on G.hn interfaces that are currently the Domain Master, i.e. for which parameter {{param|#.IsDM}} is {{true}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the {{object}}.

parameter.name: BandNumber
parameter.description: The masked band number.

parameter.name: StartSubCarrier
parameter.description: Index of the lowest frequency sub-carrier in the band to be masked as specified in {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-79}}. This parameter is writable only on the interface which acts as the Domain Master.

parameter.name: StopSubCarrier
parameter.description: Index of the highest frequency sub-carrier in the band to be masked as specified in Table 8-79 in {{bibref|G.9961}}. This parameter is writable only on the interface which acts as the Domain Master.

object.name: Device.Ghn.Diagnostics.
object.description: The G.hn Diagnostics object.

command.name: PHYThroughput()
command.description:
G.hn PHY throughput diagnostics configuration and results.
When diagnostics are requested, all G.hn nodes for which the {{param|#.Interface.{i}.PHYThroughputDiagnosticsEnable}} parameter is set enter PHY diagnostics mode.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: The interface over which the test is to be performed.

parameter.name: DiagnoseMACAddress
parameter.description:
The MAC address of the originating G.hn interface of the link that is being diagnosed.
Note: This MAC address might belong to another node of the domain.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. {{enum}}
If the value of this parameter is anything other than {{enum|Complete}}, the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

object.name: Result.{i}.
object.description: PHY throughput diagnostics results.

parameter.name: DestinationMACAddress
parameter.description: MAC address of the destination node of the link being measured.

parameter.name: LinkState
parameter.description: Indicates the state of the link between the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|#.DiagnoseMACAddress}} and the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|DestinationMACAddress}}.

parameter.name: TxPhyRate
parameter.description: PHY data rate in transmit direction in the link between the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|#.DiagnoseMACAddress}} and the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|DestinationMACAddress}}. It is represented in {{units}} as defined in Note 1 to {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-48}}. To convert from the value in the table, divide by 32K (32768) and round down.

parameter.name: RxPhyRate
parameter.description: PHY data rate in receive direction in the link between the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|#.DiagnoseMACAddress}} and the G.hn Interface with MAC address {{param|DestinationMACAddress}}. It is represented in {{units}} as defined in Note 1 to {{bibref|G.9961|Table 8-48}}. To convert from the value in the table, divide by 32K (32768) and round down.

command.name: PerformanceMonitoring()
command.description:
G.hn Performance Monitoring diagnostics configuration and results.
When diagnostics are requested, all G.hn nodes for which the {{param|#.Interface.{i}.PerformanceMonitoringDiagnosticsEnable}} parameter is set enter PHY diagnostics mode.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: The interface over which the test is to be performed.

parameter.name: DiagnoseMACAddress
parameter.description:
The MAC address of the originating G.hn interface of the link that is being diagnosed.
Note: This MAC address might belong to another node of the domain.

parameter.name: SampleInterval
parameter.description:
Time in {{units}} between automatic collection of performance monitoring data. A value of zero disables automatic collection of data.
The node MAY impose a minimum sample interval, in which case an attempt to set a (non-zero) interval that is less than this minimum MUST set the interval to the minimum and MUST NOT be regarded as an error.
If SampleInterval is a simple fraction of a day, e.g. 900 (a quarter of an hour) or 3600 (an hour), the device MAY choose to align sample intervals with time of day, but is not required to do so.

parameter.name: SNRGroupLength
parameter.description: The number of sub-carriers in a group to be used for averaging SNR values when providing SNR information for a channel.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. {{enum}}
If the value of this parameter is anything other than {{enum|Complete}}, the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

object.name: Nodes.
object.description:
Per-node G.hn performance monitoring results.
When automatic collection is enabled, i.e. {{param|#.SampleInterval}} is non-zero, the "current" interval is defined by the most recent automatic sample and the most recent subsequent manual sample, if any.
When automatic collection is disabled, i.e. SampleInterval is zero, the "current" interval is defined by the three most recent manual samples.
Note: Packets in statistics counters are Ethernet packets.

parameter.name: CurrentStart
parameter.description:
Start time for the current interval.
When automatic collection is enabled, i.e. SampleInterval is non-zero, the current interval started at the most recent automatic sample.
When automatic collection is disabled, i.e. SampleInterval is zero, the current interval started two manual samples ago.

parameter.name: CurrentEnd
parameter.description:
End time for the current interval.
When automatic collection is enabled, i.e. SampleInterval is non-zero, the current interval ended at the most recent manual sample since the most recent automatic sample. If there has been no such manual sample, the current interval is empty.
When automatic collection is disabled, i.e. SampleInterval is zero, the current interval ended at the most recent manual sample.

object.name: Nodes.Node.{i}.
object.description:
Per-node G.hn performance monitoring results during the current sample interval. Each table entry contains the results collected between the G.hn nodes with MAC addresses {{param|##.DiagnoseMACAddress}}) and {{param|DestinationMACAddress}}).
Note: Packet counters indicate the number of packets received between {{param|#.CurrentStart}} and {{param|#.CurrentEnd}}.

parameter.name: DestinationMACAddress
parameter.description: MAC address of the destination node of the link being measured.

parameter.name: BytesSent
parameter.description:
The total number of MPDU bytes transmitted or retransmitted by the node through a physical medium (i.e., PMI defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}), which correspond to data LPDUs (i.e., data packets) and framing overhead (e.g., LFH, LPH, LPCS defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1}}). It does not include transmitted bytes contributed by management LPDUs (i.e., management packets).
Note: LPDUs in mixed LLC frame blocks are considered data LPDUs.

parameter.name: BytesReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of MPDU bytes received by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to data LPDUs and framing overhead. It does not include received bytes contributed by management LPDUs. It might include blocks with errors.
Note: LPDUs in mixed LLC frame blocks are considered data LPDUs.

parameter.name: PacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}) that were transmitted by the node through the physical medium. It does not include transmitted LCDUs.

parameter.name: PacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) that were received by the node through the physical medium. It does not include received LCDUs.

parameter.name: ErrorsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}). This parameter represents the total number of LCDUs requested for transmission by a management layer (i.e., outbound LCDUs generated in LLC defined in in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1.3}}) that were transmitted by the node through a physical medium) but could not be transmitted because of errors (e.g., APDUs containing CRC errors).

parameter.name: ErrorsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received APDUs that contained errors preventing them from being delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point defined in {{bibref|G.9960|Clause 5.2.1}}). The possible causes of error are: incorrect CRC, incorrect MIC, incorrect MIC size, and incorrect size of packet.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a unicast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a unicast address at this layer.

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) but chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being transmitted (e.g., buffer overflow).

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received APDUs that were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being delivered.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs that were requested for transmission by a higher layer (i.e., outbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer. It includes APDUs that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received APDUs that were delivered to a higher layer (i.e., inbound APDUs at the x1 reference point) and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer.

parameter.name: UnknownProtoPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of APDUs received by the management that were discarded because of an unknown or unsupported protocol.

parameter.name: MgmtBytesSent
parameter.description: The total number of MPDU bytes transmitted by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to management LPDUs and framing overhead.

parameter.name: MgmtBytesReceived
parameter.description: The total number of MPDU bytes received by the node through a physical medium, which correspond to management LPDUs and framing overhead.

parameter.name: MgmtPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of LCDUs requested for transmission by a management layer (i.e., outbound LCDUs generated in LLC defined in {{bibref|G.9961|Clause 8.1.3}}) that were transmitted by the node through a physical medium.

parameter.name: MgmtPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of LCDUs delivered to a management layer (i.e., inbound LCDUs) that were received by the node through a physical medium.

parameter.name: BlocksSent
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were transmitted by the node through a physical medium, regardless of new or retransmitted LPDUs.

parameter.name: BlocksReceived
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were received by the node through a physical medium, with or without errors.

parameter.name: BlocksResent
parameter.description: The total number of LPDUs that were retransmitted.

parameter.name: BlocksErrorsReceived
parameter.description:
The total number of received LPDUs that contained errors.
Note the following relationships hold:
* PacketsSent + ErrorsSent + DiscardPacketsSent = UnicastPacketsSent + MulticastPacketsSent + BroadcastPacketsSent.
* PacketsReceived = UnicastPacketsReceived + MulticastPacketsReceived + BroadcastPacketsReceived.
* Retransmission rate = BlocksResent / BlocksSent.
* Block error rate = BlocksErrorReceived / BlocksReceived.

object.name: Channels.
object.description:
Per-channel G.hn performance monitoring results.
Note: channels are unidirectional.

parameter.name: TimeStamp
parameter.description: Time at which channel data was last collected.

object.name: Channels.Channel.{i}.
object.description: Per-channel G.hn performance monitoring results during the current sample interval. Each table entry contains the results collected from the channel between a G.hn interface (as indicated by {{param|##.DiagnoseMACAddress}}) and a G.hn interface indicated by {{param|DestinationMACAddress}})

parameter.name: DestinationMACAddress
parameter.description: MAC address of the destination node of the link being measured.

parameter.name: SNR
parameter.description: The result of an SNR test performed over the channel. It is formatted as a comma-separated list of N/M unsigned integers that represents the result of Signal-to-Noise-Ratio measurement (in {{units}}) averaging in groups of M subcarriers. The number N depends on the bandplan used by the node and corresponds to the OFDM control parameter N of each medium as defined in {{bibref|G.9964}}. The number M corresponds to the parameter {{param|##.SNRGroupLength}}.

object.name: Device.HomePlug.
object.description: HomePlug object that contains the {{object|Interface}} table. The HomePlug industry standard {{bibref|HPAV1.1}} defines peer to peer communication over powerline medium.

parameter.name: InterfaceNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.HomePlug.Interface.{i}.
object.description: HomePlug interface table (a stackable interface object as described in {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2}}). Each table entry models the PHY and MAC levels of a HomePlug interface {{bibref|HPAV1.1}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description:
Enables or disables the interface.
This parameter is based on ''ifAdminStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
The current operational state of the interface (see {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.2}}). {{enum}}
When {{param|Enable}} is {{false}} then {{param}} SHOULD normally be {{enum|Down}} (or {{enum|NotPresent}} or {{enum|Error}} if there is a fault condition on the interface).
When {{param|Enable}} is changed to {{true}} then {{param}} SHOULD change to {{enum|Up}} if and only if the interface is able to transmit and receive network traffic; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Dormant}} if and only if the interface is operable but is waiting for external actions before it can transmit and receive network traffic (and subsequently change to {{enum|Up}} if still operable when the expected actions have completed); it SHOULD change to {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} if and only if the interface is prevented from entering the {{enum|Up}} state because one or more of the interfaces beneath it is down; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|Error}} state if there is an error or other fault condition detected on the interface; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|NotPresent}} state if the interface has missing (typically hardware) components; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Unknown}} if the state of the interface can not be determined for some reason.
This parameter is based on ''ifOperStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.
Because the interface includes layer 1, the {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} value SHOULD never be used.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: The textual name of the interface as assigned by the CPE.

parameter.name: LastChange
parameter.description: The accumulated time in {{units}} since the interface entered its current operational state.

parameter.name: LowerLayers
parameter.description:
{{list}} {{reference|an interface object that is stacked immediately below this interface object}} See {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.1}}.
Note: Since {{object}} is a layer 1 interface, it is expected that {{param}} will not be used.

parameter.name: Upstream
parameter.description:
Indicates whether the interface points towards the Internet ({{true}}) or towards End Devices ({{false}}).
For example:
* For an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all WAN interfaces and {{false}} for all LAN interfaces.
* For a standalone WiFi Access Point that is connected via Ethernet to an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for the Ethernet interface and {{false}} for the WiFi Radio interface.
* For an End Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all interfaces.

parameter.name: MaxBitRate
parameter.description: The maximum upstream and downstream PHY bit rate supported by this interface (expressed in {{units}}).

parameter.name: Type
parameter.description: The type of HomePlug interface.

enumeration.description: Indicates that this is a physical HomePlug interface embedded in the Device.

Indicates that this is a logical HomePlug interface that operates over an Ethernet interface.
It is used for gathering statistics from HomePlug devices in the network and should be used when no embedded HomePlug interface is available in the Device.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: The Layer 2 Ethernet Interface over which the network protocol operates, when the Type parameter is {{enum|Logical|Type}}.

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description:
The MAC Address of the interface.
Note: This is not necessarily the same as the Ethernet header source or destination MAC address, which is associated with the IP interface and is modeled via the {{param|##.Ethernet.Link.{i}.MACAddress}} parameter.

parameter.name: LogicalNetwork
parameter.description: The textual name of the HomePlug Logical Network.

parameter.name: Version
parameter.description:
Indicates the HomePlug version of the interface. This element SHOULD be in the form of dot-delimited integers, where each successive integer represents a more minor category of variation. For example:
: "1.0"
: "1.1"

parameter.name: FirmwareVersion
parameter.description: The firmware version of the interface.

parameter.name: ForceCCo
parameter.description:
Central Coordinator (CCo) selection mode.
If {{false}}, CCo selection is automatic. If {{true}}, the local HomePlug interface is forced to be CCo and all other devices in the Logical Network MUST be set to automatic CCo selection.
Typically {{param}} is set to automatic CCo selection ({{false}}).

parameter.name: NetworkPassword
parameter.description: The network password of the device. This is a human readable ASCII string that is hashed per the HomePlug specification to generate the Network Membership Key (NMK). Note that care needs to be taken when setting this parameter as it might prohibit communication with other adapters or equipment connected via the powerline network.

parameter.name: OtherNetworksPresent
parameter.description:
{{list}} Indicates whether any other HomePlug networks are currently visible via this interface. Examples of valid list items include, but are not limited to:
: "HomePlugAV"
: "HomePlug1.0"
: "Other"

parameter.name: AssociatedDeviceNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.HomePlug.Interface.{i}.Stats.
object.description:
Throughput statistics for this interface.
The CPE MUST reset the interface's Stats parameters (unless otherwise stated in individual object or parameter descriptions) either when the interface becomes operationally down due to a previous administrative down (i.e. the interface's {{param|#.Status}} parameter transitions to a down state after the interface is disabled) or when the interface becomes administratively up (i.e. the interface's {{param|#.Enable}} parameter transitions from {{false}} to {{true}}). Administrative and operational interface status is discussed in {{bibref|TR-181i2|section 4.2.2}}.

command.name: Reset()
command.description: Reset all this object's statistics counters to zero.

parameter.name: BytesSent
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} transmitted out of the interface, including framing characters.

parameter.name: BytesReceived
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} received on the interface, including framing characters.

parameter.name: PacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} transmitted out of the interface.

parameter.name: PacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} received on the interface.

parameter.name: ErrorsSent
parameter.description: The total number of outbound {{units}} that could not be transmitted because of errors.

parameter.name: ErrorsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of inbound {{units}} that contained errors preventing them from being delivered to a higher-layer protocol.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} requested for transmission which were not addressed to a multicast or broadcast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of outbound {{units}} which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being transmitted. One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.

parameter.name: DiscardPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of inbound {{units}} which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being delivered. One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} that higher-level protocols requested for transmission and which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: UnicastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were not addressed to a multicast or broadcast address at this layer.

parameter.name: MulticastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were addressed to a multicast address at this layer.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} that higher-level protocols requested for transmission and which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer, including those that were discarded or not sent.

parameter.name: BroadcastPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of received {{units}}, delivered by this layer to a higher layer, which were addressed to a broadcast address at this layer.

parameter.name: UnknownProtoPacketsReceived
parameter.description: The total number of {{units}} received via the interface which were discarded because of an unknown or unsupported protocol.

parameter.name: MPDUTxAck
parameter.description: HomePlug-specific statistic. The Number of MAC Protocol Data Units (MPDUs) Transmitted and Acknowledged.

parameter.name: MPDUTxCol
parameter.description: HomePlug-specific statistic. The Number of MAC Protocol Data Units (MPDUs) Transmitted and Collided

parameter.name: MPDUTxFailed

parameter.name: MPDURxAck

parameter.name: MPDURxFailed
parameter.description: HomePlug-specific statistic. The Number of MAC Protocol Data Units (MPDUs) Received and Failed

parameter.description:
{{list}} List items represent MAC addresses of end stations bridged by the remote HomePlug device.
For example: "11:22:33:AA:BB:CC, 22:33:44:DD:EE:66"

object.name: Device.UPA.Interface.{i}.
object.description: UPA interface table (a stackable interface object as described in {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2}}). Each table entry models the PHY and MAC levels of a UPA interface {{bibref|UPA-PLC}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description:
Enables or disables the interface.
This parameter is based on ''ifAdminStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
The current operational state of the interface (see {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.2}}). {{enum}}
When {{param|Enable}} is {{false}} then {{param}} SHOULD normally be {{enum|Down}} (or {{enum|NotPresent}} or {{enum|Error}} if there is a fault condition on the interface).
When {{param|Enable}} is changed to {{true}} then {{param}} SHOULD change to {{enum|Up}} if and only if the interface is able to transmit and receive network traffic; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Dormant}} if and only if the interface is operable but is waiting for external actions before it can transmit and receive network traffic (and subsequently change to {{enum|Up}} if still operable when the expected actions have completed); it SHOULD change to {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} if and only if the interface is prevented from entering the {{enum|Up}} state because one or more of the interfaces beneath it is down; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|Error}} state if there is an error or other fault condition detected on the interface; it SHOULD remain in the {{enum|NotPresent}} state if the interface has missing (typically hardware) components; it SHOULD change to {{enum|Unknown}} if the state of the interface can not be determined for some reason.
This parameter is based on ''ifOperStatus'' from {{bibref|RFC2863}}.
Because the interface includes layer 1, the {{enum|LowerLayerDown}} value SHOULD never be used.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: The textual name of the interface as assigned by the CPE.

parameter.name: LastChange
parameter.description: The accumulated time in {{units}} since the interface entered its current operational state.

parameter.name: LowerLayers
parameter.description:
{{list}} {{reference|an interface object that is stacked immediately below this interface object}} See {{bibref|TR-181i2|Section 4.2.1}}.
Note: Since {{object}} is a layer 1 interface, it is expected that {{param}} will not be used.

parameter.name: Upstream
parameter.description:
Indicates whether the interface points towards the Internet ({{true}}) or towards End Devices ({{false}}).
For example:
* For an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all WAN interfaces and {{false}} for all LAN interfaces.
* For a standalone WiFi Access Point that is connected via Ethernet to an Internet Gateway Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for the Ethernet interface and {{false}} for the WiFi Radio interface.
* For an End Device, {{param}} will be {{true}} for all interfaces.

parameter.name: MaxBitRate
parameter.description: The maximum upstream and downstream PHY bit rate supported by this interface (expressed in {{units}}).

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description:
The MAC Address of the interface.
Note: This is not necessarily the same as the Ethernet header source or destination MAC address, which is associated with the IP interface and is modeled via the {{param|##.Ethernet.Link.{i}.MACAddress}} parameter.

parameter.name: FirmwareVersion
parameter.description: This interface's firmware version.

parameter.name: NodeType
parameter.description: Type of UPA device role. It can be Fixed Access Point (master) or End Point (slave) of the PLC network. {{enum}}

parameter.name: LogicalNetwork
parameter.description: The name (network ID) of the logical PLC network in which the local interface is a member (human readable string).

parameter.name: EncryptionMethod
parameter.description: Encryption Method used by UPA device. {{enum}}

parameter.name: EncryptionKey
parameter.description:
Encryption key for secure PLC communications.
This a human readable string used by the system to generate the encryption key to encrypt communications in powerline. It takes non extended ASCII characters (i.e. printable 7-bit ASCII character codes 32-126, which includes SPACE but excludes TAB, LF and CR). For example: bvjPekZiYUf9kjNKJASkgJ09adfoP01Fjvgd

parameter.name: PowerBackoffEnabled
parameter.description: Power back-off management feature status in the UPA device. Boolean can be {{true}} for "enabled" and {{false}} for "disabled".

parameter.name: PowerBackoffMechanismActive
parameter.description: Show if power back-off mechanism is active at that time in the UPA device. Boolean can be {{true}} for "active" and {{false}} for "not active".

parameter.name: EstApplicationThroughput
parameter.description: The estimated application throughput (expressed in {{units}}), received from the PLC link. This value can be used to indicate link quality.

parameter.name: ActiveNotchEnable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the {{object|ActiveNotch}} table for this interface.

parameter.description: {{numentries}}

Administrative and operational interface status is discussed in {{bibref|TR-181i2|section 4.2.2}}.

object.name: Device.UPA.Interface.{i}.AssociatedDevice.{i}.
object.description: This table contains information about PLC connections running between this UPA interface and other UPA devices.

parameter.name: MACAddress
parameter.description: Remote UPA device MAC address.

parameter.name: Port
parameter.description: The PLC port number.

parameter.name: LogicalNetwork
parameter.description:
The name of the logical PLC network (human readable string).
In the case where the associated device belongs to a different powerline network than the UPA interface, the actual network identifier of the neighboring network is not shown in {{param}}. Rather, only a generic string, e.g. "Network 1", "Network 2", etc is stored here due to security/privacy implications.

parameter.name: PhyTxThroughput
parameter.description: Physical transmission throughput (in {{units}}).

parameter.name: PhyRxThroughput

parameter.name: RealPhyRxThroughput
