Identifies the method of traffic measurement to be used for this policer.
{{enum|SimpleTokenBucket}} makes use of {{param|CommittedRate}} and {{param|CommittedBurstSize}}.
{{enum|SingleRateThreeColor}} makes use of {{param|CommittedRate}}, {{param|CommittedBurstSize}}, and {{param|ExcessBurstSize}} as defined in {{bibref|RFC2697}}.
{{enum|TwoRateThreeColor}} makes use of {{param|CommittedRate}}, {{param|CommittedBurstSize}}, {{param|PeakRate}}, and {{param|PeakBurstSize}} as defined in {{bibref|RFC2698}}.

parameter.name: PossibleMeterTypes
parameter.description: {{list}} Indicates supported meter types.

parameter.name: ConformingAction
parameter.description:
Instructions for how to handle traffic that is conforming. {{pattern}}
{{pattern|Null}} corresponds with no action.
''<DSCP Value>'' is an unsigned integer that corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP with the configured DSCP.
''<:Ethernet Priority>'' is a colon (":") followed by an unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's Ethernet Priority with the configured Ethernet Priority.
''<DSCP Value:Ethernet Priority>'' is an unsigned integer followed by a colon (":") and a second unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP and Ethernet Priority with the configured values.
For example, "24" specifies a DSCP value of 24, ":3" specifies an Ethernet Priority of 3, and "24:3" specifies both.

parameter.name: PartialConformingAction
parameter.description:
Instructions for how to handle traffic that is partially conforming (colored yellow). {{pattern}}
{{pattern|Null}} corresponds with no action.
''<DSCP Value>'' is an unsigned integer that corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP with the configured DSCP.Only applies for three-color meters.
''<:Ethernet Priority>'' is a colon (":") followed by an unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's Ethernet Priority with the configured Ethernet Priority.
''<DSCP Value:Ethernet Priority>'' is an unsigned integer followed by a colon (":") and a second unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP and Ethernet Priority with the configured values.
For example, "24" specifies a DSCP value of 24, ":3" specifies an Ethernet Priority of 3, and "24:3" specifies both.

parameter.name: NonConformingAction
parameter.description:
Instructions for how to handle traffic that is non-conforming. {{pattern}}
{{pattern|Null}} corresponds with no action.
''<DSCP Value>'' is an unsigned integer that corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP with the configured DSCP.
''<:Ethernet Priority>'' is a colon (":") followed by an unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's Ethernet Priority with the configured Ethernet Priority.
''<DSCP Value:Ethernet Priority>'' is an unsigned integer followed by a colon (":") and a second unsigned integer (no white space). It corresponds with a mark action overwriting the traffic's DSCP and Ethernet Priority with the configured values.
For example, "24" specifies a DSCP value of 24, ":3" specifies an Ethernet Priority of 3, and "24:3" specifies both.

parameter.name: TotalCountedPackets
parameter.description: Total number of Packets counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: TotalCountedBytes
parameter.description: Total number of Bytes counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: ConformingCountedPackets
parameter.description: Number of conforming Packets counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: ConformingCountedBytes
parameter.description: Number of conforming Bytes counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: PartiallyConformingCountedPackets
parameter.description: Number of partially conforming Packets counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: PartiallyConformingCountedBytes
parameter.description: Number of partially conforming Bytes counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: NonConformingCountedPackets
parameter.description: Number of non-conforming Packets counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

parameter.name: NonConformingCountedBytes
parameter.description: Number of non-conforming Bytes counted by this policer, regardless of meter action.

object.name: Device.QoS.Queue.{i}.
object.description:
Queue table. Each entry is associated with a set of traffic classes, which are specified via the {{param|TrafficClasses}} parameter, and is configured with weight, precedence, drop algorithm, scheduler algorithm etc as appropriate for the traffic classes. An entry can be associated either with all egress interfaces (in which case an actual queue will be instantiated on each egress interface on which traffic of that traffic class can be generated) or else with a single specified egress interface.
For enabled table entries, if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference and {{param|AllInterfaces}} is {{false}}, then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this queue.

parameter.name: Status
Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Children
parameter.description: {{list}} Each reference can be associated with another {{object|##.QoS.Queue.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Shaper.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Scheduler.{i}}} instance object. The references in this parameter are used to build a hierarchy.

parameter.name: TrafficClasses
parameter.description:
{{list}} Each list item identifies the set of traffic classes associated with this queue.
Traffic is sent to this queue if a {{object|#.Classification}}, {{object|#.App}} or {{object|#.Flow}} table entry specifies a traffic class, e.g. via the {{param|#.Classification.{i}.TrafficClass}} parameter.
If more than one queue on a given egress interface is associated with a given traffic class, the implementation will choose which queue to send traffic of this class to.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description:
{{reference}} Specifies the egress interface for which the specified queue MUST exist.
This MAY be a layer 1, 2 or 3 interface, however, the types of interfaces for which ''Queues'' can be instantiated is a local matter to the CPE.

parameter.name: AllInterfaces
parameter.description: Indicates that the specified queue MUST exist for all egress interfaces (i.e. this queue entry is to apply to all egress interfaces). If {{true}}, the value of {{param|Interface}} is ignored since all egress interfaces are indicated.

parameter.name: HardwareAssisted
parameter.description: Indicates whether ''all'' the queues corresponding to this table entry are hardware assisted. If any of the queues corresponding to this table entry are not hardware assisted, the parameter value MUST be {{false}}.

parameter.name: BufferLength
parameter.description:
Number of {{units}} in the buffer.
Queue buffer size for all egress interfaces for which this queue exists. If the buffer size is not the same for all such egress interfaces, this parameter MUST be 0.

parameter.name: Weight
parameter.description: Weight of this queue in case of {{enum|WFQ|SchedulerAlgorithm}} or {{enum|WRR|SchedulerAlgorithm}}, but only used for queues of equal precedence.

parameter.name: Precedence
parameter.description: Precedence of this queue relative to others. Lower numbers imply greater precedence.

parameter.name: REDThreshold
parameter.description:
Random Early Detection threshold, used only when {{param|DropAlgorithm}} is {{enum|RED|DropAlgorithm}}.
This is the minimum threshold (''min_th'') and is measured as a percentage of the queue size. If the value is set to zero, the CPE MUST choose a sensible value, e.g. 5 (but the value MUST still read back as zero).
In this version of the data model, there is no way to set the maximum threshold (''max_th''). The CPE MUST choose a sensible value, e.g. three times the minimum threshold.
In this version of the data model, there is no way to set the RED weight (''w_q''). The CPE MUST choose a sensible value, e.g. 0.002.

parameter.name: REDPercentage
parameter.description:
Random Early Detection percentage, used only when {{param|DropAlgorithm}} is {{enum|RED|DropAlgorithm}}.
This is the maximum value of the packet marking probability (''max_p''). If the value is set to zero, the CPE MUST choose a sensible value, e.g. 10 (but the value MUST still read back as zero).
In this version of the data model, there is no way to set the RED weight (''w_q''). The CPE MUST choose a sensible value, e.g. 0.002.

parameter.name: DropAlgorithm
parameter.description: Dropping algorithm used for this queue if congested.

enumeration.description: Random Early Detection {{bibref|RED}}
Drop Tail
Weighted RED
{{bibref|BLUE}}

parameter.name: SchedulerAlgorithm
parameter.description: Scheduling Algorithm used by scheduler.

enumeration.description: Weighted Fair Queueing
Weighted Round Robin
Strict Priority

parameter.name: ShapingRate
parameter.description:
Rate to shape this queue's traffic to. For leaky bucket (constant rate shaping), this is the constant rate. For token bucket (variable rate shaping), this is the average rate.
If <= 100, in percent of the rate of the highest rate-constrained layer over which the packet will travel on egress.
If > 100, in bits per second.
A value of -1 indicates no shaping.
For example, for packets destined for a WAN DSL interface, if the egress will be on a PPP or IP link with a specified ''ShapingRate'', the percentage is calculated relative to this rate. Otherwise, if the ATM layer is rate-constrained, then the rate is calculated relative to this rate. Otherwise, the rate is calculated relative to the physical-layer DSL rate.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: CurrentShapingRate
parameter.description:
If the Queue is active, the CurrentShapingRate must reflect the actual configured ShapingRate, in {{units}} per second. -1 means no rate due to do Queue not active.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: AssuredRate
parameter.description:
Minimum rate to shape this queue's traffic to.
If <= 100, in percent of the rate of the highest rate-constrained layer over which the packet will travel on egress.
If > 100, in bits per second.
A value of -1 indicates no shaping.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: CurrentAssuredRate
parameter.description:
If the Queue is active, the CurrentAssuredRate must reflect the actual configured AssuredRate, in bits per second. -1 means no rate due to do Queue not active.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: ShapingBurstSize
parameter.description: Burst size in {{units}}. For both leaky bucket (constant rate shaping) and token bucket (variable rate shaping) this is the bucket size and is therefore the maximum burst size.

object.name: Device.QoS.QueueStats.{i}.
object.description:
Queue statistics table. This table is managed by the Controller, which will create entries only for those {Queue, Interface} combinations for which statistics are to be collected.
Note: The {{object}} table includes unique key parameters that are strong references. If a strongly referenced object is deleted, the CPE will set the referencing parameter to {{empty}}. However, doing so under these circumstances might cause the updated {{object}} row to then violate the table's unique key constraint; if this occurs, the CPE MUST disable the offending {{object}} row.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this object.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description: The status of this object.

enumeration.description: Enabled and {Queue,Interface} is valid
Enabled but {Queue,Interface} is invalid

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Queue
parameter.description: {{reference}} Indicates ''Queue'' entry with which this object is associated.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description:
{{reference}} Specifies the egress interface for which this object contains statistics.
This MAY be a layer 1, 2 or 3 interface, however, the types of interfaces for which ''QueueStats'' can be instantiated is a local matter to the CPE.

parameter.name: OutputPackets
parameter.description: Number of packets output through the queue.

parameter.name: OutputBytes
parameter.description: Number of {{units}} output through the queue.

parameter.name: DroppedPackets
parameter.description: Number of packets dropped by the queue.

parameter.name: DroppedBytes
parameter.description: Number of {{units}} dropped by the queue.

parameter.name: QueueOccupancyPackets
parameter.description: Queue occupancy in packets (gives a measure of queue latency).

parameter.name: QueueOccupancyPercentage
parameter.description: Queue occupancy measured as a {{units}}, i.e. 100 * queue occupancy in bytes / queue size in bytes (gives a measure of queue usage).

object.name: Device.QoS.Shaper.{i}.
object.description:
Shaper table. Used to shape the queue(s) associated with {{param|Interface}}. In case of a single queue for that interface, determines the egress rate of the queue. In case of multiple queues for that interface (possibly with per queue shaping rates), determines the aggregate egress rate on that interface.
For enabled table entries, if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.
Note: The {{object}} table includes a unique key parameter that is a strong reference. If a strongly referenced object is deleted, the CPE will set the referencing parameter to {{empty}}. However, doing so under these circumstances might cause the updated {{object}} row to then violate the table's unique key constraint; if this occurs, the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}} and disable the offending {{object}} row.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this shaper.

parameter.name: Status
Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Children
parameter.description: {{list}} Each reference can be associated with another {{object|##.QoS.Queue.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Shaper.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Scheduler.{i}}} instance object. The references in this parameter are used to build a hierarchy.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: {{reference}}The interface object associated with this ''Shaper'' entry. It MAY be a layer 1, 2 or 3 interface, however, the types of interfaces for which ''Shapers'' can be instantiated is a local matter to the CPE.

parameter.name: ShapingRate
parameter.description:
Rate to shape the associated interface connection's egress traffic to. For leaky bucket (constant rate shaping), this is the constant rate. For token bucket (variable rate shaping), this is the average rate.
If <= 100, in percent of the rate of the highest rate-constrained layer over which the packet will travel on egress.
If > 100, in bits per second.
A value of -1 indicates no shaping.
For example, for packets destined for a WAN DSL interface, if the ATM layer is rate-constrained, then the rate is calculated relative to this rate. Otherwise, the rate is calculated relative to the physical-layer DSL rate.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: ShapingBurstSize
parameter.description: Burst size in {{units}}. For both leaky bucket (constant rate shaping) and token bucket (variable rate shaping) this is the bucket size and is therefore the maximum burst size.

object.name: Device.QoS.Scheduler.{i}.
object.description: Scheduler table. Each entry is used to model a scheduler object.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this scheduler.

parameter.name: Status
Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Children
parameter.description: {{list}} Each reference can be associated with another {{object|##.QoS.Queue.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Shaper.{i}}}, {{object|##.QoS.Scheduler.{i}}} instance object. The references in this parameter are used to build a hierarchy.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description:
{{reference}} Specifies the egress interface for which the specified queue MUST exist.
This MAY be a layer 1, 2 or 3 interface, however, the types of interfaces for which ''Queues'' can be instantiated is a local matter to the CPE.

parameter.name: SchedulerAlgorithm
parameter.description: Scheduling Algorithm used by scheduler.

enumeration.description: Weighted Fair Queueing
Weighted Round Robin
Strict Priority

parameter.name: ShapingRate
parameter.description:
Rate to shape this scheduler's traffic to. For leaky bucket (constant rate shaping), this is the constant rate. For token bucket (variable rate shaping), this is the average rate.
If <= 100, in percent of the rate of the highest rate-constrained layer over which the packet will travel on egress.
If > 100, in bits per second.
A value of -1 indicates no shaping.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: AssuredRate
parameter.description:
Minimum guaranteed rate to shape this scheduler's traffic to.
Must be > 0 and < ShapingRate, for a valid rate.
A value of -1 indicates the ShapingRate's value is not used.
Note: To be able to support higher bit rates, this parameter was changed to unsignedLong in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: DefaultQueue

object.name: Device.LANConfigSecurity.
object.description: This object contains generic device configuration information.

parameter.name: ConfigPassword
parameter.description:
A password to allow LAN access to protected auto-configuration services.
If the CPE supports TR-064 (LAN-side DSL CPE Configuration Protocol), this parameter is to be used as the ''dslf-config'' password (as defined in TR-064).
If the CPE has a user interface with password protection enabled, this parameter is also to be used as the user password for password-protected operations. However, this parameter MUST NOT be used to set the user password if the parameter {{param|#.UserInterface.PasswordUserSelectable}} is {{true}}.

object.name: Device.Hosts.
object.description: This object provides information about each of the hosts on the LAN, including those whose IP address was allocated by the CPE using DHCP as well as hosts with statically allocated IP addresses. It can also include non-IP hosts.

parameter.name: HostNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: CleanupHostsThreshold
parameter.description:
Specifies the threshold related to the number of Host entries that are retained in the {{object|Device.Hosts.Host.{i}.}} table.
If this threshold is exceeded, the device removes the inactive Host entry with the oldest {{param|Host.{i}.ActiveLastChange}} timestamp that is, the Host entry for which {{param|Host.{i}.Active}} is {{false}} and the host entry for which has been inactive the longest.
A value of '-1' disables this mechanism.

parameter.name: AccessControlNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

command.name: RemoveInactiveHosts()
command.description:
Removes Host entries where {{param|Host.{i}.Active}} is {{false}}, and the Host has been inactive for longer than {{param|MinimumInactiveTime}}.
The inactivity duration is calculated based on the {{param|Host.{i}.ActiveLastChange}} timestamp.

parameter.name: MinimumInactiveTime
parameter.description:
Specifies the minimum duration, in {{units}}, for which a Host must be inactive before being removed.
When {{param}} is not specified, all inactive Host entries are removed.

parameter.name: NumberOfRemovedHosts
parameter.description: Indicates the total number of hosts successfully removed.

object.name: Device.Hosts.Host.{i}.
object.description: Host table.

parameter.name: Alias
PhysAddress
parameter.description: Unique physical identifier of the host. For many layer 2 technologies this is typically a MAC address.

parameter.name: IPAddress
parameter.description:
Current IP Address of the host. {{empty}} if no address is available.
If more than one IP address for this host is known, the CPE will choose a ''primary'' address. All known IP addresses can be listed in the {{object|IPv4Address}} and {{object|IPv6Address}} tables.

parameter.name: AddressSource
DHCPClient
parameter.description: {{reference}} Each list item is the DHCPv4 or DHCPv6 server's client entry that corresponds to the host.

parameter.name: LeaseTimeRemaining
AssociatedDevice
parameter.description:
{{noreference}}The value MUST be the path name of the ''AssociatedDevice'' (or equivalent) table row that models the host, or {{null}} if either there is no such table or the host isn't directly connected to this device (e.g. the host is connected to a Wi-Fi Access Point).
For example: ''Device.WiFi.AccessPoint.1.AssociatedDevice.2''

parameter.name: Layer1Interface
parameter.description:
{{noreference}}The value MUST be the path name of a row in a layer 1 interface table. If either the layer 1 interface isn't known or the host isn't directly connected to this device (e.g. the host is connected to a Wi-Fi Access Point), then {{param}} will be {{null}}.
For example: ''Device.Ethernet.Interface.2''

parameter.name: Layer3Interface
parameter.description: {{reference}} If either the layer 3 interface isn't known or the host isn't directly connected to this device (e.g. the host is connected to a Wi-Fi Access Point), then {{param}} will be {{null}}.

parameter.name: InterfaceType
parameter.description: Type of physical interface through which this host is connected.

parameter.name: VendorClassID
ClientID
UserClassID
HostName
parameter.description: The device's host name or {{empty}} if unknown.

parameter.name: Active
parameter.description:
Whether or not the host is currently present on the LAN. The method of presence detection is a local matter to the CPE.
The ability to list inactive hosts is OPTIONAL. If the CPE includes inactive hosts in this table, {{param}} MUST be set to {{false}} for each inactive host. The length of time an inactive host remains listed in this table is a local matter to the CPE.
Entries in Device.Hosts.Host SHOULD NOT be removed when they become inactive if there are {{object|WANStats}} statistics collected for the entry in the past seven days, unless requested by a Controller or if the {{param|#.CleanupHostsThreshold}} parameter value is reached.

parameter.name: ActiveLastChange
parameter.description:
The datetime when {{param|Active}} last changed from {{true}} to {{false}} or from {{false}} to {{true}}. The initial detection of a host SHOULD be treated as a transition from {{false}} to {{true}}, showing the datetime when the host was first detected.
The ability to list inactive hosts is OPTIONAL. The length of time an inactive host remains listed in this table is a local matter to the CPE.
Entries in Device.Hosts.Host SHOULD NOT be removed when they become inactive if there are {{object|WANStats}} statistics collected for the entry in the past seven days, unless requested by a Controller or if the {{param|#.CleanupHostsThreshold}} parameter value is reached.

parameter.name: IPv4AddressNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: IPv6AddressNumberOfEntries

parameter.name: BytesReceived
parameter.description: The total number of bytes received from the WAN and sent to the Host device at the IP layer.

parameter.name: PacketsSent
parameter.description: The total number of IP packets transmitted to the WAN from the Host device.

parameter.name: ErrorsSent
parameter.description: The total number of outbound IP packets to the WAN from the Host device that could not be transmitted because of errors. These may be due to the number of retransmissions exceeding the retry limit, or from other causes.

object.name: Device.Hosts.AccessControl.{i}.
object.description:
Every instance of this object provides access control for a LAN device.
Access is allowed if no instance of {{object}} is defined for a device.
If access is not allowed, then the LAN device cannot access the broadband network.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Origin
parameter.description:
Indicates the owner of the {{object}} instance.
Note: This parameter was changed to writeOnceReadOnly in the Device:2.18 version.

enumeration.description: Used for indicating that the access control rule was created by the end-user. For example through the web user interface.
Used for indicating that the access control rule was created by the system itself.
Used for indicating that the access control rule was created by a Controller.

parameter.name: PhysAddress
parameter.description: Unique physical identifier of the device. For many layer 2 technologies this is typically a MAC address.

parameter.name: PhysAddressMask
parameter.description:
Mask to be applied on {{param|PhysAddress}}. When set to 'FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF' the access control rule is applicable to a single host. Other possible values 'FF:FF:FF:00:00:00' to apply access control to a specific OUI.
When {{empty}} is set, no mask will be applied and the {{param|PhysAddress}} MUST be used as is.

parameter.name: HostName
parameter.description: Any user defined name for the device.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this {{object}} entry.

parameter.name: AccessPolicy
parameter.description:
Allows or denies access for a device.
If {{param}} is set to "Allow", device access is allowed based on the {{object|.Schedules.Schedule}} objects referenced by the {{param|ScheduleRef}} parameter. Access is enabled if there is no {{object|.Schedules.Schedule}} object referenced by the {{param|ScheduleRef}} parameter.
If {{param}} is set to "Deny", {{object|.Schedules.Schedule}} objects referenced by the {{param|ScheduleRef}} parameter are ignored and no access is allowed for the device.

parameter.name: ScheduleRef
parameter.description: Each reference provides a time schedule that controls when the associated feature or resource is active or inactive. When {{param}} is {{empty}} the {{object}} is not scheduled, and the {{param|Enable}} defines the operational state.

parameter.name: ScheduleNumberOfEntries

object.name: Device.Hosts.AccessControl.{i}.Schedule.{i}.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this {{object}} entry.

parameter.name: Day
parameter.description: {{list|the days for which access is enabled}} {{enum}}

parameter.name: StartTime
parameter.description:
Start time of the enable schedule in hh:mm format. [hh] refers to a zero-padded hour between 00 and 23. [mm] refers to a zero-padded minute between 00 and 59.
Start time is in local time zone.

parameter.name: Duration
parameter.description:
The duration, in {{units}}, which the access is enabled.
If the {{param|StartTime}} is not defined, duration is the total time access is allowed during a calendar day.
If a {{param|StartTime}} is defined, access is allowed for the {{param}} period starting from {{param|StartTime}}.

object.name: Device.DNS.Diagnostics.
object.description: The DNS Diagnostics object containing the {{command|NSLookupDiagnostics()}} test.

command.name: NSLookupDiagnostics()
command.description:
This command defines access to an IP-layer NS Lookup test for the specified IP interface.
When initiated, the NS Lookup test will contact {{param|DNSServer}} and look up {{param|HostName}} {{param|NumberOfRepetitions}} times.
There will be a {{object|Result}} instance for each time the device performs a DNS lookup, which is determined by the value of {{param|NumberOfRepetitions}}.
Any previous {{object|Result}} instances are removed when a new test is initiated.

parameter.name: Interface
HostName
parameter.description: Specifies the Host Name that NS Lookup is to look for. The current domain name MUST be used unless the name is a fully qualified name.

parameter.name: DNSServer
parameter.description:
Specifies the DNS Server name or IP address that NS Lookup is to use for the lookup. The name of this server will be resolved using the default DNS server unless an IP address is provided.
If {{empty}} is specified, the device's default DNS server will be used.

parameter.name: Timeout
parameter.description: Timeout in {{units}} that indicates that a request has failed.

parameter.name: NumberOfRepetitions
parameter.description:
The number of times the device SHOULD repeat the execution of the NSLookup using the same input parameters. If the diagnostics test fails the CPE MAY terminate the test without completing the full number of repetitions.
Each repetition will use a Result instance to hold the NSLookup result data.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description:
Indicates the availability of diagnostics data. {{enum}}
If the value of this parameter is anything other than {{enum|Complete}}, the values of the other results parameters for this test are indeterminate.

enumeration.description: Unable to resolve DNSServer Name

parameter.name: SuccessCount
parameter.description: Number of successfully executed repetitions.

object.name: Result.{i}.
object.description: Results from the most recent invocation of the test, one instance per repetition.

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description: Result Parameter to represent whether the NS Lookup was successful or not.

parameter.name: AnswerType
parameter.description: Result parameter to represent whether the answer is Authoritative or not.

enumeration.description: Indicates that the NS Lookup failed to find the host.

parameter.name: HostNameReturned
IPAddresses
parameter.description: {{list}} Indicates the IP Address results returned by the NS Lookup; if no response was provided, then this parameter is {{empty}}.

parameter.name: DNSServerIP
parameter.description: Result parameter to represent the actual DNS Server IP address that the NS Lookup used.

parameter.name: ResponseTime
parameter.description: Response time (for the first response packet) in {{units}}, or 0 if no response was received.

object.name: Device.DNS.SD.Advertise.{i}.
object.description:
The {{object}} table contains DNS-SD services that MUST be advertised. DNS.SD service information is provided in DNS RR SRV records {{bibref|RFC2782}}. The Service Instance Name {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1 Structured Instance Names}} further specifies information about the service name (RFC2782 Service field) and domain name (RFC2782 Name field) in the form:
Service Instance Name = [InstanceName] . [Service] . [Domain]
[Service] = _[ApplicationProtocol] . _[TransportProtocol]
RFC2782 Service field will always be equal to [InstanceName]. [Service]
RFC2782 Name field will always be equal to [Domain]
For example, an SSH service might have:
*{{param|InstanceName}} = "Secure Shell (SSH))"
*{{param|ApplicationProtocol}} = "ssh"
*{{param|TransportProtocol}} = "TCP"
*{{param|Port}} = 22

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the advertisement of the DNS-SD service.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Status
parameter.description: The status of the advertised {{object}}.

enumeration.description: Indicates that the DNS-SD service advertisement is disabled.
Indicates that the DNS-SD service advertisement is enabled.
Indicates that a necessary configuration value is undefined or invalid.
MAY be used to define an error condition.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description:
{{reference}} The layer 3 interface on which the DNS-SD service MUST be advertised. Example: ''Device.IP.Interface.1'' or ''Device.Logical.Interface.1''.
{{template|INTERFACE-ROUTING}}

parameter.name: InstanceName
parameter.description:
Human-readable instance name {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.1 Instance Names}} (i.e. The "[{{param}}]" portion of the '"Service Instance Name'").
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: ApplicationProtocol
parameter.description:
The Application Protocol, without the leading underscore, associated with the service (e.g., daap) as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 7 Application Protocol Names}}.
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: TransportProtocol
parameter.description:
The Transport Protocol associated with the service as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.2 Service Names}}.
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: Domain
parameter.description:
The value to be entered into the Name field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}} which represents the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) associated with the service as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.3 Domain Names}}.
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: Port
parameter.description:
The value to be entered into the Port field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}} that is used to contact the service.
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: TextRecordNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.DNS.SD.Advertise.{i}.TextRecord.{i}.
object.description:
This object maintains an instance of a (key/value pairs) of the service. The information is to be provided in the DNS TXT records {{bibref|RFC1035}} of the advertised service.
When multiple instances of the {{object}} table have the same value for the {{param|Key}} parameter, the implementation is CPE specific.
Note: This object was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: Key
parameter.description: The key that identifies the text record

parameter.name: Value
parameter.description: The value of the text record.

object.name: Device.DNS.SD.Service.{i}.
object.description:
The {{object}} table contains discovered DNS-SD services. DNS.SD service information is provided in DNS RR SRV records {{bibref|RFC2782}}. The Service Instance Name {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1 Structured Instance Names}} further specifies information about the service name (RFC2782 Service field) and domain name (RFC2782 Name field) in the form:
Service Instance Name = [InstanceName] . [Service] . [Domain]
[Service] = _[ApplicationProtocol] . _[TransportProtocol]
RFC2782 Service field will always be equal to [InstanceName]. [Service]
RFC2782 Name field will always be equal to [Domain]
For example, an SSH service might have:
*{{param|InstanceName}} = "Secure Shell (SSH))"
*{{param|ApplicationProtocol}} = "ssh"
*{{param|TransportProtocol}} = "TCP"
*{{param|Domain}} = "example.com"
*{{param|Port}} = 22
*{{param|Target}} = "ssh.example.com."

parameter.name: InstanceName
parameter.description: Human-readable instance name {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.1 Instance Names}} (i.e. The "[{{param}}]" portion of the '"Service Instance Name'").

parameter.name: ApplicationProtocol
parameter.description: The Application Protocol, without the leading underscore, associated with the service (e.g., daap) as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 7 Application Protocol Names}}.

parameter.name: TransportProtocol
parameter.description: The Transport Protocol associated with the service as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.2 Service Names}}.

parameter.name: Domain
parameter.description: The value extracted from the Name field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}} which represents the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) associated with the service as defined by the DNS-SD service {{bibref|DNS-SD|Section 4.1.3 Domain Names}}.

parameter.name: Port
parameter.description: The value extracted from the Port field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}} that is used to contact the service.

parameter.name: Target
parameter.description: The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) with the trailing dot "." of the target host implementing the service as in the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}}.

parameter.name: Status

enumeration.description: The {{object}} has received a response record with TTL > 0 and the {{param|#.Service.{i}.TimeToLive}} has not expired yet. The {{object}} is considered active.
The device has received a response record containing TTL=0 indicating a goodbye message and the {{param|#.Service.{i}.TimeToLive}} has not expired yet. The {{object}} is considered inactive.
The {{param|#.Service.{i}.TimeToLive}} has expired. The {{object}} is considered inactive

parameter.name: LastUpdate
parameter.description: The date and time at which the last advertisement for this {{object}} was received.

parameter.name: Host
parameter.description: Includes all Host table entries, active or inactive, that correspond to this discovered DNS.SD service.

parameter.name: TimeToLive
parameter.description: The value extracted from the TTL field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}}.

parameter.name: Priority
parameter.description: The value extracted from the Priority field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}}.

parameter.name: Weight
parameter.description: A server selection mechanism. The value extracted from the Weight field of the DNS SRV record {{bibref|RFC2782}} that specifies the relative weight for entries with the same {{param|Priority}}.

object.name: Device.DNS.RebindProtection.
object.description:
The DNS Rebind Protection object contains parameters to enable or disable protection against DNS rebind attacks.
It prevents DNS-based malicious software that tries to bypass the browser’s policies, by filtering or refusing DNS answers that point to private or local IP addresses, it stops external sites from reaching LAN devices.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or Disables protection against DNS rebind attacks

parameter.name: IPExceptions
parameter.description: Each item of the list represents an IP address or a CIDR notation that should not be protected against rebind attacks.

parameter.name: DomainExceptions
parameter.description: Each item of the list represents a domain name and its subdomain names that should not be protected against rebind attacks.

object.name: Device.NAT.
object.description:
Properties for Network Address Translation (NAT).
The entire {{object}} object only applies to IPv4.

parameter.name: InterfaceSettingNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: PortMappingNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: MaxNumberOfPortMappings
parameter.description:
The maximum number of port mappings that can exist at any given time.
If the value of this parameter is 0, then it means that the device doesn't have a limit to the number of port mappings that can exist.

parameter.name: PortTriggerNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: MaxNumberOfPortTriggers
parameter.description:
The maximum number of port triggers that can exist at any given time.
If the value of this parameter is 0, then it means that the device doesn't have a limit to the number of port mappings that can exist.

object.name: Device.NAT.InterfaceSetting.{i}.
object.description:
NAT settings for an associated IP Interface on which NAT is enabled.
For enabled table entries, if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.
Note: The {{object}} table includes a unique key parameter that is a strong reference. If a strongly referenced object is deleted, the CPE will set the referencing parameter to {{empty}}. However, doing so under these circumstances might cause the updated {{object}} row to then violate the table's unique key constraint; if this occurs, the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}} and disable the offending {{object}} row.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the {{object}} entry, indicating if NAT is enabled for the referenced IP Interface instance. On creation, an {{object}} entry is disabled by default.

parameter.name: Status

enumeration.description: NAT enabled but forced by a third party to be operationally disabled, e.g. because a {{object|##.MAP.Domain}} is enabled but there is no Basic Mapping Rule {{bibref|RFC7597}}.
NAT enabled but port mapping has been operationally disabled by a third party, e.g. because this is REQUIRED by the current {{object|##.Firewall}} level.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: {{reference}} The associated outgoing IP interface on which NAT is to be enabled.

parameter.name: SourceNetwork
parameter.description:
Each list item MUST be the Path name of a {{object|.IP.Interface.{i}.IPv4Address.}} table or of one of its rows. If the referenced object is deleted, the corresponding item MUST be removed from the list.
Specifies the source IPv4 network(s) that MUST be translated for all outgoing traffic associated with the {{param|Interface}} (e.g. ''Device.IP.Interface.2.IPv4Address.'' (table) or ''Device.IP.Interface.2.IPv4Address.1.'' (row)).
The {{param|.IP.Interface.{i}.IPv4Address.{i}.IPAddress}} and {{param|.IP.Interface.{i}.IPv4Address.{i}.SubnetMask}} are used to construct an additional filter rule that specifies which address range needs to be translated.

parameter.name: TCPTranslationTimeout
parameter.description: Determines the timeout, in {{units}}, of NAT translations for TCP sessions. It is the time after which a NAT entry is removed from the NAT table if there is no activity. A value of -1 represents an infinite duration.

parameter.name: UDPTranslationTimeout
parameter.description: Determines the timeout, in {{units}}, of NAT translations for UDP bindings. It is the time after which a NAT entry is removed from the NAT table if there is no activity. A value of -1 represents an infinite duration.

object.name: Device.NAT.PortMapping.{i}.
object.description:
Port mapping table.
This table MUST contain all NAT port mappings associated with this connection, including static and dynamic port mappings programmatically created via local control protocol, such as UPnP.
This table MUST NOT contain dynamic NAT binding entries associated with the normal operation of NAT.
If the CPE hosts a firewall, it is assumed that it will appropriately configure the firewall for the port mapping.
For enabled table entries, if {{param|InternalClient}} is {{empty}}, or if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference and {{param|AllInterfaces}} is {{false}}, then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the port mapping instance. On creation, an entry is disabled by default.

parameter.name: Status

enumeration.description: Indicates that the port mapping is still enabled but has been temporarily deactivated due to the Schedules defined in {{param|ScheduleRef}}.

parameter.name: Origin
parameter.description:
Indicates the Origin of the {{object}} instance.
Note: This parameter was changed to writeOnceReadOnly in the Device:2.18 version.

enumeration.description: Used for indicating that the port mapping entry was created by the end-user. For example through the web user interface.
Used for indicating that the port mapping entry was created by the system itself.
Used for indicating that the port mapping entry was created by a device using UPnP-IGD.
Used for indicating that the port mapping entry was created by a Controller.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description:
{{datatype|expand}}
Note: There is no guarantee that the {{param}} value on automatically-created {{object}} instances will be retained. This is because automatically-created {{object}} instances can be transitory.

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: {{reference}} Specifies the IP interface to which this port mapping applies.

parameter.name: AllInterfaces
LeaseDuration
parameter.description:
Determines the time to live, in {{units}}, of a port mapping lease, where "time to live" means the number of {{units}} before the port mapping expires.
A value of 0 means the port mapping is static. Support for dynamic (non-static) port mappings is OPTIONAL. That is, the only value for {{param}} that MUST be supported is 0.
For a dynamic (non-static) port mapping, when this parameter is read, the value is the same as when the {{object}} was created. Note: the Device:2.19 version of the data model moved the dynamic countdown behavior, when reading the {{param}}, to the {{param|RemainingLeaseTime}}.

parameter.name: RemainingLeaseTime
parameter.description:
For a dynamic (non-static) port mapping, when this parameter is read, the value represents the time (in {{units}}) remaining on the port mapping lease. That is, for a dynamic port mapping, the value counts down toward 0. When a dynamic port mapping lease expires, the device MUST automatically terminate that port mapping, and MUST automatically delete the corresponding {{object}} table entry.
For a static port mapping, this parameter is irrelevant and should return ''0''.

parameter.name: RemoteHost
ExternalPort
ExternalPortEndRange
parameter.description:
Indicates the last port of the external port range that starts with {{param|ExternalPort}}.
If an external port range is specified, then the behavior described for {{param|ExternalPort}} applies to all ports within the range.
A value of zero (0) indicates that no external port range is specified, i.e. that the range consists only of {{param|ExternalPort}}.
If {{param|ExternalPort}} is zero (wildcard), the value of this parameter MUST be ignored.
If specified, the value of this parameter MUST be greater than or equal to the value of {{param|ExternalPort}}.

parameter.name: InternalPort
parameter.description:
The port on {{param|InternalClient}} that the gateway SHOULD forward traffic to.
When {{param|ExternalPortEndRange}} is utilized, this range will also be applied accordingly, starting from the {{param}} number.
Example: ExternalPort=3000 and ExternalPortEndRange=3010 with InternalPort=5000 means the ports are mapped as follows:
* External port 3000 maps to internal port 5000
* External port 3001 maps to internal port 5001
* External port 3002 maps to internal port 5002
* ...
* External port 3010 maps to internal port 5010

parameter.name: Protocol
parameter.description: The protocol of the port mapping. {{enum}}

parameter.name: InternalClient
parameter.description:
The IP address or DNS host name of an internal client (on the LAN).
Support for an IP address is mandatory. If {{param}} is specified as an IP address and the LAN device's IP address subsequently changes, the port mapping MUST remain associated with the original IP address.
Support for DNS host names is OPTIONAL. If {{param}} is specified as a DNS host name and the LAN device's IP address subsequently changes, the port mapping MUST remain associated with this LAN device. In this case, it is the responsibility of the CPE to maintain the name-to-address mapping in the event of IP address changes. This can be accomplished, for example, by assigning the DNS host name via use of DHCP option 12 (Host Name) or option 81 (FQDN). Note that the Controller can learn the host name associated with a given LAN device via the {{object|##.Hosts.Host}} table.
Read access to this parameter MUST always return the exact value that was last set by the Controller. For example, if the internal client is set to a DNS host name, it MUST read back as a DNS host name and not as an IP address.
It MUST be possible to set the {{param}} to the broadcast IP address 255.255.255.255 for UDP mappings. This is to enable multiple NAT clients to use the same well-known port simultaneously.

parameter.name: Description
parameter.description: User-readable description of this port mapping.

parameter.name: ScheduleRef
parameter.description: Each reference provides a time schedule that controls when the associated feature or resource is active or inactive. When {{param}} is {{empty}} the {{object}} is not scheduled, and the {{param|Enable}} defines the operational state.

parameter.name: Log
parameter.description: Enable or disable logging, in a {{object|.DeviceInfo.VendorLogFile}}, of packets matching this {{object}}.

parameter.name: LogRef
parameter.description: Specifies the logging rules for this {{object}} entry. The {{param|Log}} parameter MUST be set to {{true}} for this setting to take effect. When {{param|Log}} is {{true}} and {{param}} is {{empty}} or contains an invalid reference, the system MUST treat the configuration as an error and set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.

If {{param|Port}} is zero, the value of this parameter MUST be ignored.

parameter.name: AutoDisableDuration
parameter.description: Number of {{units}} the port trigger MUST be active. When the {{param}} is expired new connections are no longer allowed, active connections SHOULD not be terminated.

parameter.name: ActivationDate

Indicates when the port trigger was enabled. When the port trigger is no longer active.
Note: This parameter was demoted to readOnly in the Device:2.18 version.

parameter.name: Protocol

parameter.name: ScheduleRef
parameter.description: Each reference provides a time schedule that controls when the associated feature or resource is active or inactive. When {{param}} is {{empty}} the {{object}} is not scheduled, and the {{param|Enable}} defines the operational state.

parameter.name: Log
parameter.description: Enable or disable logging, in a {{object|.DeviceInfo.VendorLogFile}}, of packets matching this {{object}}.

parameter.name: LogRef
parameter.description: Specifies the logging rules for this {{object}} entry. The {{param|Log}} parameter MUST be set to {{true}} for this setting to take effect. When {{param|Log}} is {{true}} and {{param}} is {{empty}} or contains an invalid reference, the system MUST treat the configuration as an error and set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.

object.name: Device.PCP.
object.description:
Properties for Port Control Protocol (PCP) {{bibref|RFC6887}}.
See the PCP Theory of Operation {{bibref|TR-181i2|Appendix XIV}} for a description of the working of this PCP data model.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the PCP stack. If the stack is disabled then the status of any enabled {{object|Client}} entries will change to {{enum|StackDisabled|Client.{i}.Status}}.

parameter.name: SupportedVersions
parameter.description:
{{list}} Each list item denotes a PCP version supported by the PCP Client. Currently known versions are 0, 1 and 2.
This parameter is based on Version from {{bibref|RFC6887}}.

parameter.name: PreferredVersion
parameter.description:
This is the version to be used in the first exchange with a new PCP Server.
The factory default MUST be the highest supported version, as described in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 9}}.

parameter.name: OptionList
parameter.description: {{list}} The list of the PCP Options supported by the PCP Client.

parameter.name: ClientNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.
object.description: Client properties for Port Control Protocol (PCP). The PCP Client interacts with a PCP Server as defined in {{bibref|RFC6887}} for internal device applications or LAN device applications via Interworking functions.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the PCP Client.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: WANInterface
parameter.description: {{reference|the interface stack instance representing the WAN interface this client operates on}} See {{object|##.InterfaceStack}}

parameter.name: Status
MAPEnable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the MAP OpCode.

parameter.name: PEEREnable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the PEER OpCode.

parameter.name: ANNOUNCEEnable
parameter.description:
Enables or disables the ANNOUNCE OpCode.
When {{false}} the PCP Client does not support unsolicited ANNOUNCE messages.

parameter.name: THIRDPARTYEnable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the THIRD_PARTY Option.

parameter.name: THIRDPARTYStatus
FILTEREnable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the FILTER option.

parameter.name: ServerNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.PCPProxy.
object.description: Properties for the Port Control Protocol (PCP) Proxy, as specified in {{bibref|PCPProxy}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the PCP Proxy for this PCP Client.

parameter.name: HighestVersion
parameter.description:
A string identifying the highest version of PCP that the proxy supports.
This parameter is based on Version from {{bibref|RFC6887}}.

parameter.name: Status

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.UPnPIWF.
object.description: Properties for the interworking function between UPnP IGD (Internet Gateway Device) and PCP, as specified in {{bibref|RFC6970}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the UPnP IGD-PCP Interworking Function for this PCP Client.

parameter.name: Status

The status of the UPnP IGD-PCP Interworking Function for this PCP Client. {{enum}}
The {{enum|Error}} value MAY be used by the CPE to indicate a locally defined error condition.

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.Server.{i}.
object.description:
This table contains the PCP Servers to be used by the PCP Client. Entries are either statically configured or automatically created via DHCP options OPTION_V4_PCP_SERVER and OPTION_V6_PCP_SERVER, as per {{bibref|RFC7291}}.
Each OPTION_V4_PCP_SERVER or OPTION_V6_PCP_SERVER option corresponds to a {{object}} instance. If an option returns multiple addresses then that {{object}} instance has multiple addresses.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this PCP Server.

parameter.name: Status
Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Origin
parameter.description:
Method used to assign {{param|ServerNameOrAddress}} and create this table entry. {{enum}}
Note: In the {{enum|DHCPv4}} and {{enum|DHCPv6}} cases, if more than one IP address is received {{param|ServerNameOrAddress}} will be the first address and {{param|AdditionalServerAddresses}} will be the remaining addresses.

enumeration.description: {{param|ServerNameOrAddress}} is an IPv4 address that was received via OPTION_V4_PCP_SERVER
{{param|ServerNameOrAddress}} is an IPv6 address that was received via OPTION_V6_PCP_SERVER

{{param|ServerNameOrAddress}} is an FQDN, IPv4 address or IPv6 address that was created by the Controller, by some other management entity (e.g. via a GUI), or is present in the factory default configuration

parameter.name: ServerNameOrAddress
parameter.description: The FQDN or IP address of the PCP Server, assigned as described under {{param|Origin}}.

parameter.name: ServerAddressInUse
parameter.description:
The IP address currently in use for the PCP Server, derived from the value of {{param|ServerNameOrAddress}}.
{{empty}} indicates that no PCP Server address is currently known.

parameter.name: AdditionalServerAddresses
parameter.description: PCP Server addresses in addition to {{param|ServerNameOrAddress}}. This can be non-empty only if {{param|Origin}} is {{enum|DHCPv4|Origin}} or {{enum|DHCPv6|Origin}} and if more than one PCP Server address was received.

parameter.name: ExternalIPAddress
parameter.description: The external IP address of the PCP-controlled device hosting this server.

parameter.name: CurrentVersion
parameter.description:
This is the version of PCP resulting from client-server Version Negotiation.
This parameter is based on Version from {{bibref|RFC6887}}.

parameter.name: MaximumFilters
parameter.description: Indicates the maximum number of inbound filters allowed to be associated with a mapping entry on this server.

parameter.name: PortQuota
parameter.description:
Indicates the maximum number of ports allocated to this PCP Client on this server.
A value of 0 means that there is no limitation.

parameter.name: PreferredLifetime
parameter.description: Indicates the preferred lifetime (in {{units}}) to be used for mappings with this server when no preference is selected by an application/user.

parameter.name: Capabilities
parameter.description: Indicates the capabilities supported by the PCP Server. {{enum}}

parameter.name: InboundMappingNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: OutboundMappingNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.Server.{i}.InboundMapping.{i}.
object.description:
Inbound Mapping table.
This table contains all Inbound Mappings requested by this PCP Client on this PCP Server. Such a mapping is created by a PCP request with OpCode MAP, as described in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 11}}.
These requests can be issued from internal device applications, from static configuration or from other LAN device applications via interworking functions such as UPnP IGD or PCP proxies. The {{param|Origin}} parameter indicates which mechanism requested the mapping.
For non-{{enum|Static|Origin}} mappings (here ''Static'' refers to the mechanism that created the mapping, not to the {{param|Lifetime}}), the Controller MAY modify the {{param|Enable}} parameter but MUST NOT modify any other parameters in the mapping or its sub-objects.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this {{object}} instance.

parameter.name: Status
ErrorCode
parameter.description: Provides the PCP error code when {{param|Status}} is {{enum|Error_PCPErrorCodeReceived|Status}}. Error code values are defined in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 7.4}}.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Origin
parameter.description: Mechanism via which the mapping was requested. {{enum}}

enumeration.description: Requested via internal device application
Requested via UPnP IGD interworking function
Requested via PCP proxy
Requested via static configuration, i.e. created by the Controller, by some other management entity (e.g. via a GUI), or is present in the factory default configuration

parameter.name: Lifetime
parameter.description:
Determines the time to live, in {{units}}, of this Inbound Mapping lease, i.e. the remaining time before this port mapping expires.
A value of 0 means that the port mapping is permanent (referred to as a static mapping in {{bibref|RFC6887}}).
When a dynamic Inbound Mapping lease expires, the CPE MUST automatically delete the corresponding {{object}} table entry.

parameter.name: SuggestedExternalIPAddress
parameter.description:
The external IPv4 or IPv6 Address that the PCP-controlled device will listen on for incoming packets to be forwarded to the PCP Client.
This is useful for refreshing an Inbound Mapping, especially after the PCP Server loses state. If the PCP client does not know the external address, or does not have a preference, it MUST use {{empty}}.

parameter.name: SuggestedExternalPort
parameter.description:
The external port (or the first port of a range of external ports) that the PCP-controlled device will listen on for incoming packets. Those inbound packets will be forwarded to {{param|InternalPort}}. If the PCP client does not know the external port, or does not have a preference, it MUST use 0.
This is useful for refreshing an Inbound Mapping, especially after the PCP Server loses state. If the PCP Client does not know the external port, or does not have a preference, it MUST use 0.

parameter.name: SuggestedExternalPortEndRange
parameter.description:
Indicates the last port of the external port range that starts with {{param|SuggestedExternalPort}}.
If an external port range is specified, then the behavior described for {{param|SuggestedExternalPort}} applies to all ports within the range.
A value of zero (0) indicates that no external port range is specified, i.e. that the range consists only of {{param|SuggestedExternalPort}}.
If {{param|SuggestedExternalPort}} is zero (wildcard), the value of {{param}} MUST be ignored.
If specified, the value of this parameter MUST be zero or be greater than or equal to the value of {{param|SuggestedExternalPort}}.

parameter.name: InternalPort
parameter.description: The port on this PCP Client's {{param|##.WANInterface}} that the PCP-controlled device forwards incoming packets to.

parameter.name: ProtocolNumber
parameter.description:
The protocol number of the {{object}}. Values are taken from {{bibref|IANA-protocolnumbers}}.
The value -1 means ''all protocols''.

parameter.name: ThirdPartyAddress
parameter.description:
Under certain conditions, the PCP Client can create a PCP mapping on behalf of another device, by using the THIRD_PARTY option, as specified in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 7.3}}. In that case, {{param}} is the IP address of the device for which the PCP operation is requested.
For non-third-party mappings, {{param}} SHOULD be {{empty}}.

parameter.name: Description
parameter.description: User-readable description of this {{object}}.

parameter.name: AssignedExternalIPAddress
parameter.description: The external IPAddress returned by the PCP Server. The IP address that the PCP-controlled device is listening on for incoming packets to a corresponding PCP Client.

parameter.name: AssignedExternalPort
parameter.description: The external port returned by the PCP Server. The external port (or the first port of a range of external ports) that the PCP-controlled device is listening on for incoming packets to a corresponding {{param|InternalPort}}. Inbound packets to this external port on the External interface of the PCP-controlled device is forwarded to the on the {{param|InternalPort}}.

parameter.name: AssignedExternalPortEndRange
parameter.description:
Indicates the last port of the external port range that starts with {{param|AssignedExternalPort}}.
If an external port range is specified, then the behavior described for {{param|AssignedExternalPort}} applies to all ports within the range.
A value of zero (0) indicates that no external port range is specified, i.e. that the range consists only of {{param|AssignedExternalPort}}.

parameter.name: FilterNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.Server.{i}.InboundMapping.{i}.Filter.{i}.
object.description:
Filter table.
This table contains all Filters restricting this Inbound Mapping, as defined in {{bibref|RFC6887|}}.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: RemoteHostIPAddress
parameter.description: Permitted remote peer IP address for this filter.

parameter.name: PrefixLength
parameter.description: Indicates how many bits of {{param|RemoteHostIPAddress}} are relevant for this filter.

parameter.name: RemotePort
parameter.description:
Permitted remote peer port number for this filter.
The value 0 indicates ''all ports''.

parameter.name: RemotePortEndRange
parameter.description:
Indicates the last port of the remote port range that starts with {{param|RemotePort}}.
If an external port range is specified, then the behavior described for {{param|RemotePort}} applies to all ports within the range.
A value of zero (0) indicates that no remote port range is specified, i.e. that the range consists only of {{param|RemotePort}}.
Note: This parameter was promoted to readWrite in the Device:2.18 version.

object.name: Device.PCP.Client.{i}.Server.{i}.OutboundMapping.{i}.
object.description:
Outbound Mapping table.
This table contains all Outbound Mappings requested by this PCP Client on this PCP Server. Such a mapping is created by a PCP request with OpCode PEER, as described in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 12}}.
These requests can be issued from internal device applications, from static configuration or from other LAN device applications via interworking functions such as UPnP IGD or PCP proxies. The {{param|Origin}} parameter indicates which mechanism requested the mapping.
For non-{{enum|Static|Origin}} mappings (here ''Static'' refers to the mechanism that created the mapping, not to the {{param|Lifetime}}), the Controller MAY modify the {{param|Enable}} parameter but MUST NOT modify any other parameters in the mapping or its sub-objects.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this {{object}} instance.

parameter.name: Status
ErrorCode
parameter.description: Provides the PCP Error code when {{param|Status}} is {{enum|Error_PCPErrorCodeReceived|Status}}. Error code values are defined in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 7.4}}.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Origin
parameter.description: Mechanism via which the mapping was requested. {{enum}}

enumeration.description: Requested via internal device application
Requested via UPnP IGD interworking function
Requested via PCP proxy
Requested via static configuration, i.e. created by the Controller, by some other management entity (e.g. via a GUI), or is present in the factory default configuration

parameter.name: Lifetime
parameter.description:
Determines the time to live, in {{units}}, of this Outbound Mapping lease, i.e. the remaining time before this port mapping expires.
A value of 0 means that the port mapping is permanent (referred to as a static mapping in {{bibref|RFC6887}}).
When a dynamic Outbound Mapping lease expires, the CPE MUST automatically delete the corresponding {{object}} table entry.

parameter.name: SuggestedExternalIPAddress
parameter.description:
The external IPv4 or IPv6 Address that the PCP-controlled device will use to send outgoing packets covered by this mapping.
This is useful for refreshing a mapping, especially after the PCP Server has lost state. If the PCP Client does not know the external address, or does not have a preference, it MUST use {{empty}}.

parameter.name: SuggestedExternalPort
parameter.description:
The external port that the PCP-controlled device will use to send outgoing packets covered by this mapping.
This is useful for refreshing a mapping, especially after the PCP Server has lost state. If the PCP Client does not know the external port, or does not have a preference, it MUST use 0.

parameter.name: RemoteHostIPAddress
parameter.description: The remote peer's IP address, as seen from the PCP Client, for this Outbound Mapping.

parameter.name: InternalPort
parameter.description: The port on PCP Client WAN Interface that the PCP-controlled device SHOULD listen to for this mapping.

parameter.name: RemotePort
parameter.description: The remote peer's port, as seen from the PCP Client, for this Outbound Mapping.

parameter.name: ProtocolNumber
parameter.description:
The protocol number of the {{object}}. Values are taken from the {{bibref|IANA-protocolnumbers}}.
The value -1 means ''all protocols''.

parameter.name: ThirdPartyAddress
parameter.description:
Under certain conditions, the PCP Client can create a PCP mapping on behalf of another device, by using the THIRD_PARTY option, as specified in {{bibref|RFC6887|Section 7.3}}. In that case, {{param}} is the IP address of the device for which the PCP operation is requested.
For non-third-party mappings, {{param}} SHOULD be {{empty}}.

parameter.name: Description
parameter.description: User-readable description of this {{object}}.

parameter.name: AssignedExternalIPAddress
parameter.description: The external IP address returned by the PCP Server. The IP address that the PCP-controlled device uses to send outgoing packets corresponding to this mapping.

parameter.name: AssignedExternalPort
parameter.description: The external port returned by the PCP Server. The port that the PCP-controlled device uses to send outgoing packets corresponding to this mapping.

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.
object.description: The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) IPv4 object {{bibref|RFC2131}}. This entire object applies to IPv4 only. It contains the {{object|Client}}, {{object|Server}}, and {{object|Relay}} objects.

parameter.name: ClientNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.Client.{i}.
object.description:
This object contains DHCP client settings for an associated ''IP Interface'' indicated by {{param|Interface}}.
For enabled table entries, if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}.
Note: The {{object}} table includes a unique key parameter that is a strong reference. If a strongly referenced object is deleted, the CPE will set the referencing parameter to {{empty}}. However, doing so under these circumstances might cause the updated {{object}} row to then violate the table's unique key constraint; if this occurs, the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}} and disable the offending {{object}} row.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables the DHCP Client entry.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Interface
parameter.description: {{reference}} The IP Interface associated with the ''Client'' entry.

parameter.name: Status
DHCPStatus
parameter.description:
The DHCP Client status as defined in {{bibref|RFC2131}}. {{enum}}
Note: This value is only relevant when the DHCP Client is operationally enabled (i.e. when {{param|Status}} is {{enum|Enabled|Status}}).

command.name: Renew()
command.description: The DHCP client will renew its DHCP lease.

parameter.name: IPAddress
parameter.description: IPv4 Address option received from the DHCP Server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}.

parameter.name: SubnetMask
parameter.description:
Subnet mask option received from the DHCP Server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}.
Value is information received via DHCP Option 1.

parameter.name: IPRouters
parameter.description:
{{list}} Items represent IP Router IPv4 Address(es) received from the DHCP server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}.
Value is information received via DHCP Options 3, 33 or 121.

parameter.name: DNSServers
parameter.description:
{{list}} Items represent DNS Server IPv4 Address(es) received from the DHCP server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}.
Value is information received via DHCP Option 6.

parameter.name: LeaseTimeRemaining
parameter.description: DHCP lease time remaining in {{units}}. A value of -1 indicates an infinite lease.

parameter.name: DHCPServer
parameter.description: The IPv4 address of the current DHCP server.

parameter.name: PassthroughEnable
parameter.description:
If {{false}}, the DHCP Client retrieved IP address information is configured on the referenced {{param|Interface}} object.
If {{true}}, the DHCP Client retrieved information is propagated to the parameters in the referenced {{param|PassthroughDHCPPool}} object, replacing any existing configuration (including ''MinAddress'', ''MaxAddress'', ''SubnetMask'', ''IPRouters'', and ''DNSServers'').

parameter.name: PassthroughDHCPPool
parameter.description: {{reference}}When {{param}} is set to {{empty}}, {{param|PassthroughEnable}} MUST be set to {{false}} (i.e. passthrough can not be enabled without a pool reference specified).

parameter.name: AuthenticationProtocol
parameter.description: Specifies the authentication mechanism to be used.

enumeration.description: Includes configuration token information in all DHCP messages, as defined in {{bibref|RFC3118|Section 4, Configuration Token}}.
Uses delayed authentication, as specified in {{bibref|RFC3118|Chapter 5 Delayed Authentication}}.

parameter.name: DSCPMark
parameter.description: Diffserv code point to be used for outgoing DHCP messages.

parameter.name: SentOptionNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

parameter.name: ReqOptionNumberOfEntries
parameter.description: {{numentries}}

command.name: Release()
command.description: The {{object}} will release its DHCPv4-supplied information (i.e. the Agent will send a release message to the DHCPv4 server to indicate that it will no longer use the obtained address and/or subnet).

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.Client.{i}.SentOption.{i}.
object.description: Each instance of this object represents a DHCP option that MUST, if enabled, be sent in DHCP client requests. All sent DHCP options MUST be listed.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this SentOption table entry.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Tag
parameter.description: Option tag as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132}}.

parameter.name: Value
parameter.description: A hexbinary encoded option value.

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.Client.{i}.ReqOption.{i}.
object.description: Each instance of this object represents a DHCP option that MUST, if enabled, be requested in DHCP client requests. All requested DHCP options MUST be listed.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this ReqOption table entry.

parameter.name: Order
parameter.description:
{{datatype|expand}}
This indicates the position of the option in the DHCP client request.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description: {{datatype|expand}}

parameter.name: Tag
parameter.description: Option tag as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132}}.

parameter.name: Value
parameter.description:
A hexbinary encoded, most recently received DHCP option value.
If no option value has been received, then the value MUST represent {{empty}}.
Received DHCP option values MAY, but need not, persist across CPE reboots.

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.Client.{i}.Retransmission.
object.description: This object enables the configurion of the DHCPv4 retransmission behavior according to the guidelines described in {{bibref|RFC2131|Chapter 4.1}}.

parameter.name: DiscoverInitialTimeout
parameter.description: Initial delay, expressed in {{units}}, before initiating the first DCHCPDISCOVER message.

parameter.name: DiscoverMaxTimeout
parameter.description:
Maximum duration, expressed in {{units}}, between two DHCPDISCOVER message retransmission.
According to {{bibref|RFC2131|Chapter 4.1}}, the recommended value for this parameter is 64 {{units}}.

parameter.name: DiscoverMaxDuration
parameter.description:
Maximum duration, expressed in {{units}}, during which the DHCPv4 client is permitted to retransmit DHCPDISCOVER message
A value of '0' indicates that no specific maximum duration is set.

parameter.name: RequestInitialTimeout
parameter.description: Initial delay, expressed in {{units}}, before initiating the first DHCPREQUEST message.

parameter.name: RequestMaxTimeout
parameter.description:
Maximum duration, expressed in {{units}}, between two DHCPREQUEST message retransmission.
According to {{bibref|RFC2131|Chapter 4.1}}, the recommended value for this parameter is 64 {{units}}.

parameter.name: RequestMaxDuration
parameter.description:
Maximum duration, expressed in {{units}}, during which the DHCPv4 client is permitted to retransmit DHCPREQUEST message.
A value of '0' indicates that no specific maximum duration is set.

parameter.name: TimeoutRandomize
parameter.description:
The Randomization factor for the retransmission timeout, in {{units}}, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2131|4.1 Constructing and sending DHCP messages}}.
E.g. a timeout of 2000ms with a randomization of 1000 will end up between 1000 and 3000 ms.

object.name: Device.DHCPv4.Client.{i}.Stats.

parameter.name: Discover
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPDISCOVER messages sent by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: Offer
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPOFFER messages received by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: Request
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPREQUEST messages sent by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: Decline
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPDECLINE messages sent by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: Release
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPRELEASE messages sent by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: Inform
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPINFORM messages sent by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: ACK
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPACK messages received by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: NACK
parameter.description: The total number of DHCPNACK messages received by the client, as defined in {{bibref|RFC2132|DHCP Message Type}}.

parameter.name: ForceRenew

parameter.name: DiscardedPackets

parameter.name: TransmitFailure
parameter.description: The total number of DHCP messages that failed to transmit.

command.name: Reset()
command.description: Reset all this object's statistics counters to zero.

parameter.name: Enable
